#1302. Soccer hooligans descend on Australia: Wild footage shows horde of fans smashing cars and damaging property

Published: 03:01 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 03:27 EST, 9 November 2026

Shocking footage of soccer fans after a match has reignited complaints about public safety, following previous warnings repeated violence was putting families at risk.

Perth Glory supporters have demanded action over a confrontation near HBF Park, with video posted on social media showing a group of young people as they crowded around a parked white vehicle and aggressively rocked it from side to side.

Other footage filmed from across the road shows young people confronting fans in the street, with the group spread across the footpath and roadway outside nearby businesses.

Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions, as well as damaged fences and other property. Supporters allege the material documents a recurring problem involving the same group and have demanded bans and stronger security measures.

The footage prompted calls for bans and renewed criticism of matchday security, with supporters alleging genuine fans face strict enforcement over minor issues while more serious behaviour goes unchecked.

'The same group of troublemakers causing chaos and mobbing random people', one fan posted on social media platform X.

Young people crowd around a parked white car and aggressively rock it near HBF Park in footage that has sparked anger among Perth Glory supporters

Supporters allege genuine fans are being left feeling unsafe at Perth Glory matches

Tagging Perth Glory, they added: 'It's time you do something about it. People have had enough.'

The supporter also called for individuals to be banned and, in a subsequent post, alleged nearby property had been damaged.

WA Police, Perth Glory and A-Leagues have all been contacted for comment.

Perth-based football podcast and digital channel The Far Post Perth shared the original post, adding its own demand for intervention.

'Not a good look at all and something needs to be done about the problem at this point, genuine supporters are being impacted,' the account wrote.

One commenter alleged the group had been moving through the venue during the match while being followed by security and police.

'This is the mob that was walking back and forth all game with security/police following,' they wrote.

'We don't need this at HBF Park. It makes many people feel unsafe when these wannabe thugs just shove their way through.'

Another video shows young people confronting fans on the street outside nearby businesses

Photographs of damaged fences and other property have fuelled calls for stronger action

The person who posted the footage claimed that 'after the game the police and security were nowhere to be seen'.

They also shared a separate video from February, alleging it showed an earlier confrontation involving the same group.

The February post had complained about people attending matches in The Bay supporter area and allegedly fighting with other young spectators.

The complaints follow a strongly worded statement issued last year by supporter groups The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth, which demanded sanctions after a separate incident outside Gate 2 during the second half of a match at HBF Park.

The groups said they were aware of footage circulating online and distanced themselves from those involved, alleging physical confrontations had become a recurring problem.

'We want to make it absolutely clear that those involved are not fans and do not represent our supporter groups, our values, or the wider football community,' their joint statement read.

'These individuals consistently attend matches with the sole intention of causing problems rather than supporting the team, and their behaviour is completely unacceptable.'

The statement alleged confrontations had occurred in active supporter areas and the Eastern family stand, extending the groups' concerns beyond the stadium's most vocal sections.

Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions

'In almost every single game, they have caused physical confrontations in both the Active areas, and in some cases the Eastern family stand too, and it is deeply frustrating that this behaviour continues without meaningful consequences,' the groups said.

They alleged the behaviour was damaging the experience of supporters who attended matches to follow Perth Glory.

The groups also accused matchday security provider NPB Security of failing to respond adequately to incidents.

Their criticism included allegations that a rotating contingent of inexperienced security staff was being deployed and that personnel were unable or unwilling to intervene when serious problems arose.

'The lack of accountability from NPB Security is unacceptable and has undermined the safety of the matchday environment,' the statement read.

'Warnings and passive responses are clearly not working.'

The groups called for bans and other sanctions, warning that further incidents could affect spectators and people working at the ground.

'Without firm action, including bans and real consequences, these so-called 'fans' will continue to put genuine supporters, families, and staff at risk.'

They urged the club and stadium authorities to identify those responsible and impose firm sanctions.

Their earlier warning has been followed by fresh complaints about how security rules are enforced at Perth Glory matches.

'Meanwhile security go OTT about bottled water in the shed or actual fans taking t-shirts off,' one supporter wrote in response to the latest footage.

Another commenter similarly complained that removing a shirt in the supporter bay could result in ejection, while alleging people involved in violence escaped consequences.

The Far Post Perth also challenged a response that dismissed the latest incident as 'kids being kids'.

'Kids being kids is vandalising other people's property? Interesting,' the account replied, referring to the allegations of property damage.

However, one person responding to the original footage questioned whether those shown in the street were Perth Glory supporters.

'In the second video, the person filming is standing where the stadium is. These idiots look like they are walking from the other side of the road,' the commenter wrote.

'Are we sure they are even Glory fans? Or just troublemakers.'

The person who uploaded the footage insisted they were, although the posts do not establish that the same individuals were involved in each of the incidents raised by commenters.

The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth had made their position on violence explicit in their earlier appeal for action.

'Violence, fighting, and antisocial behaviour have no place in football,' they said.

'HBF Park, The Shed, The Bay and all areas of the ground should be a safe and welcoming environment for all supporters, families, players, and staff.'

#1301. Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

“Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he said of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”

Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and said: “You held it together. You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg

For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he said. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

Kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

And he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

That work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and said he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

For the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more important than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

Kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

There's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN

Hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany said: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”

The plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has announced Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before quickly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

Aston Villa are reportedly considering a January move for Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia as Unai Emery looks to strengthen his defensive midfield options ahead of the second half of the season.

The Belgian international has emerged as a potential target for the Midlands club, which is keen to address a shortage of central midfield options after Amadou Onana’s injury.

According to a report from Fussball News, Aston Villa have been monitoring Lavia’s situation at Stamford Bridge and view the 22-year-old as a suitable candidate to reinforce their midfield in January 2027.

Emery is believed to be impressed by the Chelsea midfielder’s combination of physical strength, defensive awareness and technical ability. His capacity to protect the backline while contributing to the build-up could make him an attractive addition to Villa’s squad.

Report: Aston Villa reach verbal agreement with star wanted by Man United in summer

The report claims Villa have already explored bringing Lavia to Birmingham, with discussions reportedly taking place through intermediaries and representatives to see whether a deal is possible.

The Premier League side are understood to have a budget of approximately €35 million for the January window. However, convincing Chelsea to let the midfielder go could prove difficult.

Lavia has struggled with fitness since arriving from Southampton in 2023, but his quality in possession and ability to dictate the tempo make him a valuable option when available.

The Belgian is reportedly happy at Chelsea and is not actively pushing for an exit. Nevertheless, the prospect of securing regular first-team football could potentially persuade him to consider a new challenge.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Chelsea are under no immediate pressure to sell Lavia, especially since his current contract runs until the summer of 2030.

The Blues are not actively looking to offload the midfielder, although an attractive proposal could encourage them to reconsider.

According to the report, Chelsea could demand between €35m and €40m to sanction his departure, putting Villa’s proposed budget under considerable pressure.

Meanwhile, Emery must also consider the possibility of losing Boubacar Kamara, who has attracted interest from Inter Milan, Arsenal and Liverpool.

Losing the Frenchman would represent a significant setback for Villa, making the pursuit of Lavia potentially even more important.

The clubs have not agreed at this stage, but Villa’s interest appears serious. Much will depend on Chelsea’s willingness to negotiate and whether Lavia is open to leaving Stamford Bridge mid-campaign.

A self-confessed scriptkiddie, Taik Hobson wears many hats, not all of them necessarily green.

Fifteen miles south of Egilsstaðir, Sindri pulls over, his grin suddenly a happy thing compared with the bleak landscape outside the window.

Right. Looks no different from half an hour before, but to exit the engagement I return the smile and congratulate the father-to-be. A chatterbox, Sindri’s probably told me more than he should. I mean, married men going on about their sisters-in-law? That’s just odd.

I hop out of the truck and, watching it turn a corner, fish a compass from my jacket pocket and a map from my knapsack. Then south. Start walking. Be a good hour before the birch and snow thin out.

Blending in — it’s what hackers do. First rules, almost. Meeting street stares in Nairobi but never in Fukuoka; broadcasting it in LA but pitching down in Leipzig — something like that, but in a system. And behind a desk. No good if you can see me. For the attack, bring little: use whatever’s at hand. Live off the land, strike from the blindspots — from a system’s memory, say. If they ever catch on, I’m well in the past.

Active recon is a whole different set-up, of course, and staying invisible calls for different conditions.

That’s not a problem. The only other person who’s been in and out of Skýborg wouldn’t datum when I hit her up. Least I think it’s a her. Could be that calling ID handle √^}° a ‘guerilla hat’ — all effect, no elegance — backfired, and I shouldn’t’ve pitched it as Us vs Them. But with less than a week between Skýborg getting decommissioned and the job coming in there wasn’t more time to nose around. Never got to the ransomware business, either.

Large black squares breach the snow after the trees clear out, all nine laid flat in the space of a football field. American. Tall stick figures cross the white and that’s my signal to play it cool. Trust the conditions. The C-Skin makes it easier — had it on since Reykjavík — and crossing the perimeter I go from blue-eyed, square-jawed Icelandic youth to ebony anthropoid, complete with pulsing orb in the forehead. Instant authentication.

Security for a decommissioned cloud data centre, that’s odd, right?

DC2 in leet — or (DC)2, if you’re an A-hat — Skýborg’s underground, and even from here it looks like those traceroutes were not a glitch. Place is up and active. What’s not active is this reindeer half buried in the snow, legs up, hole in its side. Poor guy got too close to security. The irony in that is that Sindri would’ve had a better chance of spotting my black hair through the nano-refraction.

My gear’s untraceable — I’m an A-hat at heart — and the only thing brought over is a foothold I left in the system, an hour of making the deal. By now everyone’s stuffing cred on the network so maybe someone’s found it … they haven’t. The rotors retract. I’m in. In cybersec, an unknown vulnerability is called a Zero-Day threat, something everyone worries about but never expects to walk through the front door. I take the stairs, just for laughs.

Think: you put your eggs in one place then pay someone else to hold the key. Asking for it, really.

Can’t blame these guys for wanting a bigger cut. Which, oddly, isn’t what they’re asking for. Not exactly. Either more than a little green, or it’s a joke. I mean, €12.49 to unfreeze the data? But in Nepalese currency? Or have you sit while they calculate the ransom value of π. My client’s in the clear — so far. Small fry, just wants the data stored here to disappear.

Speaking of here, it’s warm. Spidey sense going off at my level. Admin left in a hurry and dumped — dumped — some of the servers. But these are … moving? Ah, right. Wow. Server-drones. Didn’t think they were real. Mobilized. Security and storage. So not the normal stint of malware then. More like aware.

Which is something I’m still working on, haha. Thought-scanners can’t catch me while my THINKbox partitions the internal dialogue, or else I’d be a pulsing white spot. And reindeer. Speaking of spots … there’s my server. It’s easy once you’re in. Use the management console to turn on the identifier lights. Now: crowbar time.

Among hats, that’s a SEDkey. Does two things: secure erases the data then degausses the whole thing. Irreversible. Looks just like a key, too. Elegant enough for you, √^}°?

All these other drones are probably wondering why I’m getting so close. Anyway, key in and …

#1298. The unexpected email that led to Bukayo Saka's Socrates Award win at the Ballon d'Or: Inside Arsenal star's secret humanitarian work after his surprise win at London ceremony

Published: 08:07 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 08:13 EST, 11 November 2026

The sight of Bukayo Saka hobbling down the red carpet at the Ballon d'Or ceremony came as a surprise. Only those closest to him knew why he was there, and the years of toil that led to this moment.

While his England team-mate Harry Kane claimed the night's top on-pitch prize, Saka – who had suffered a thigh injury just days before against Kane's Bayern Munich – was at the London Palladium to collect the Socrates Award for his humanitarian work.

Joining a roll of honour that includes previous winners Vinicius Junior, Sadio Mane and Luis Enrique, Saka walked onto the stage, reached into his suit pocket and read a letter from a 14-year-old boy in Rwanda whose eyesight had been restored through his charity work.

Now, Daily Mail Sport can reveal the scale of the Arsenal star's involvement over the last four years with the BigShoe charity, which funds operations, feeds children and helps with disaster relief across the world. From restoring the eyesight of that 14-year-old in Rwanda to helping provide life-saving procedures for 120 children in Nigeria, Saka's impact goes far beyond the stadiums he dazzles in.

And this is no passive act of philanthropy. BigShoe president Valerie Fiesser's phone is often inundated with messages from Saka when the charity is delivering projects in poverty-stricken countries such as Nigeria and Rwanda. Many of the project ideas come from the 25-year-old himself.

'Bukayo is really, really productive,' Fiesser tells Daily Mail Sport. 'He is really pushing how he wants to help. I think for him it is never fast enough to help. Sometimes Bukayo comes up with projects and he says, "Shouldn't we help here?" So he is really interested in it. It is not like he is just sending money and saying, "OK, nice, we'll do a project in Nigeria".

Bukayo Saka was handed the Ballon d'Or Socrates Award for his humanitarian work last month

Saka has worked with BigShoe charity for years - helping those in poverty-stricken countries

In 2023, Saka donated 50 containers to help provide shelter for 255 people impacted by the devastating earthquake in Morocco

'When we are on the ground, he is texting, "Is everything alright? Is everybody safe? Are all the children safe? Which services do we have? Can I see pictures? Send me pictures, send me pictures, send me pictures!"

BigShoe, a German-based charity founded during the 2006 World Cup, began years ago by funding life-changing surgery for Nourisson, a young girl from Togo born with a cleft lip and palate. The Togo national team, playing at their first World Cup, were based in the city of Wangen im Allgau, which brought the story to prominence in Germany.

The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 children around the globe having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food. The organisation has also worked with Antonio Rudiger, Paul Pogba and Saka's ex-Arsenal team-mates Mesut Ozil and Oleksandr Zinchenko.

Fiesser vividly remembers how Saka first got in touch, in early 2022.

'He just really randomly wrote us an email,' she says. 'He asked us if we can help together in Nigeria after seeing a project of another soccer player. He said, "I want to help children, I want to help people and can we do something". (It was) really just random.'

That initial conversation quickly developed into a project in late 2022 which funded 120 life-changing medical operations for children in Nigeria. Some of the youngsters were suffering from brain tumours, while others required treatment for hernias.

'This was an incredible project because it was the first project in Nigeria together with him,' she says. 'It was really life-changing for the children because some had a brain tumour, some had hernia problems.'

Saka has since helped support healthcare check-ups for more than 580 children in Rwanda and provide disaster relief after devastating earthquakes in Morocco and Turkey, while his involvement has extended far beyond financial backing.

The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 kids having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food

'We did a disaster relief where we provided homes for the earthquake victims in Morocco and Turkey and he was asking questions like, "Do they have electricity there?"' she says.

'He is really thinking, "Is it worth it, does it make sense to do this, or is it just putting the container and then the people do not have water and they cannot live there?" So he is really, really smart. And yes, I think he is an amazing human.

'It was never about him. It was always about the children and how we can help. It was never like, "OK, we are talking to one of the best players of the world." I think he is raised like this. His family made him the man he is now.

'I think he is raised like this, that you have to be a good human being and to help others and just have an impact in life.'

Saka and his family are directly involved in the projects, identifying communities in need and deciding exactly how support should be delivered. His mother, Adenike, is a key figure.

'We decide together where we can help, how we can help and then we actually help together,' Fiesser says. 'Me and his mother WhatsApp, call regularly. She has played a big part and is a driving force.

'Three months ago we renovated a school in Rwanda and we provided them with water filters for clean drinking water. We also built girls' changing rooms, a new soccer pitch and a new library. Bukayo's family was on the ground, twice.

'We decided after we saw that the families are really hungry in this area to do food packages. It is our next project in November and December.

'He (Saka) really wants to make a difference. He wants to change lives.'

While Saka will continue to chase trophies in Arsenal red and England white, his greatest legacy may ultimately be measured in the lives he has changed far beyond the football pitch.

Everton are reportedly exploring a move for Napoli midfielder Kevin De Bruyne during the January transfer window as David Moyes looks to strengthen his squad for the second half of the season.

The Belgian international has emerged as a surprise target for the Merseyside club, with his uncertain situation in Italy potentially opening the door to a return to the Premier League.

According to a Sport Witness report, Everton have already made initial contact with the player’s representatives to see whether a January transfer is feasible.

The experienced playmaker enjoyed a hugely successful spell at Manchester City, registering 108 goals and 177 assists in 422 appearances before leaving the club as a free agent in 2025.

However, his subsequent move to Napoli has not worked out as expected. The 35-year-old has struggled to find consistent form in Italy, and fitness issues have also limited his availability.

He managed five goals and four assists in 21 appearances last season and has contributed four goals and two assists in 15 matches this term.

His current situation could encourage Everton to explore bringing him back to English football.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

De Bruyne’s experience and technical ability could make him an excellent addition to Moyes’ midfield, particularly given his outstanding Premier League record.

However, convincing Napoli to sanction his departure could prove difficult. The midfielder remains under contract until 2027, with the Italian club also holding an option to extend his stay by another year.

Napoli could therefore demand a transfer fee before considering his departure mid-campaign.

Everton would need to negotiate favourable terms to complete the deal, but the opportunity to sign a player of De Bruyne’s calibre could be difficult to ignore.

#1296. ‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Ursula Martin is an emeritus professor at the Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford, UK.

In early October, the artificial-intelligence firm OpenAI posted more than 700 AI-generated mathematical manuscripts on an online public repository. The arguments — if found to be correct after verification — contain an extraordinary trove of new mathematical knowledge. The reaction to these developments from the maths community has ranged from exhilaration to despair. Some researchers worry they have spent their lifetimes attempting to solve problems and their work might now suddenly seem meaningless. Others have expressed concern about the negative impact on young colleagues who are entering the field during a period of flux. And there’s been widespread anger at the manner in which AI companies are releasing such findings.

As one of the authors of the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics, which was published in June, I think some of the field’s concerns over OpenAI’s approach to announcing its discoveries could have been anticipated. In our declaration, we did not oppose the use of AI but put forwards several practical safeguards. These included the need for clear citation policies, precise disclosures on how AI is used and a renewed commitment to the long-standing expectation that all arguments made in a maths proof should be independently verifiable and answerable by a human author. Some AI companies have agreed to follow the declaration. OpenAI has not.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow

Now that mathematicians have started analysing the AI-assisted proofs, it’s clear that many of the 700 preprints are presented in a sloppy, rough-and-ready style, making them hard to understand. The inner workings of OpenAI’s closed models are unknown, and there is also no human author named who might take responsibility for explaining or correcting the content if flaws emerge. It will take mathematicians a lot of time and effort to check the work in the preprints and rewrite it in a professional format that is suitable for judgement by peer reviewers. Unsurprisingly, many mathematicians are unenthusiastic about clearing up OpenAI’s mess, however exciting the underlying mathematics might be.

So, what does this mean for the future of mathematics? Creatively rethinking how the field must evolve will require action at every level. Outstanding leadership by individuals such as mathematician Terence Tao, and grassroots initiatives such as the Leiden declaration, need to be complemented with high-level engagement from stakeholder institutions such as the International Mathematical Union. It would be a disservice to the field if AI companies are allowed to set the norms on how to do mathematics without wide-ranging input from academics.

Arsenal are reportedly keen on a potential January transfer window deal for Real Madrid forward Endrick as they eye cover for the injured Bukayo Saka.

The Gunners failed to bring in a top class attacking player during the summer despite being linked with big names like Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers at the time, so they could do with trying again in January.

Endrick’s lack of playing time at Real Madrid could make him a serious option, and it seems Berta also has connections with the Brazil international’s representatives, according to talkSPORT.

The report suggests that Endrick is available this winter, having been offered to a number of Premier League clubs, so this certainly seems like one to watch.

Some of the details in talkSPORT’s piece are similar to what we were told about Endrick recently, with the player’s agents keen to get the 20-year-old a move this January due to his struggles at the Bernabeu.

Our understanding has been that although Arsenal have had some historic interest, they are not currently actively pursuing Endrick, with more concrete interest coming from Newcastle United, Aston Villa, and Tottenham.

One significant issue in the past has been that Real Madrid are not keen to let Endrick go, so that could still be an issue, and it might mean clubs are more likely to sign him in a straight loan deal, rather than in any kind of arrangement involving an option to buy permanently.

Endrick arrived at Real Madrid as one of the most highly-rated young talents in world football after catching the eye at Palmeiras.

A quick and skilful forward who can play up front or out wide, Endrick was well known around the world when he was still only 16, but he’s faced a lot of competition for a first-team place in Madrid.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

A loan move could be a good option for him now, and one imagines he’d be ideal to help Arsenal while Saka is out injured.

Still, if he’s struggled for minutes with Los Blancos, he needs to think carefully about his next move, and perhaps just coming in as short-term cover at another big club is not the ideal next step he needs to get his confidence and rhythm back.

#1294. Chelsea Confidential: Mike Penders' Vaseline goalkeeping hack revealed, Emi Martinez fitness update, why Estevao started against 'weak' Man United and the £750 'dressing room experience' for Blues fans

Published: 07:03 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 14:51 EST, 4 November 2026

One of the secrets to Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders stopping Manchester United from scoring at Stamford Bridge was to smear a stash of Vaseline on his goalpost.

The 21-year-old Belgian used the petroleum jelly to add grip to his gloves during the game and particularly before corners. Prior to one United set-piece, Penders walked to the woodwork to rub his hands with the substance which was hidden up high towards his crossbar. He then caught the ball when Bruno Fernandes’ cross came into his box.

It seems counterintuitive to smear a greasy substance on gloves to aid catching but it is an old goalkeeper hack – and perfectly legal in the laws of the game – with former England keeper Ben Foster once saying on his podcast: ‘It’s hard to explain, but if we were in a training session, I could tell you if one of us had Vaseline on our gloves, because as soon as I grab the ball, it does make it grippier.’

Penders may have learned the trick from Sweden’s Karl-Johan Johnsson. They were both at Chelsea’s sister side Strasbourg last season – Penders as No 1 and Johnsson as No 2.

Johnsson is now 36 and without a club. He did not respond when contacted by Confidential, but he does have an old YouTube channel. His most popular video – viewed 54,000 times and uploaded in 2021 when he was a goalkeeper for Copenhagen – is about the benefits of Vaseline.

While Johnsson would apply it from the blue-topped tub in the changing room before kick-off, he would also add a chunk to his goalpost so he could easily top up mid-match if needed.

Mike Penders has a novel trick he uses to help keep the ball out of the Chelsea net

Penders saves Ryan Gravenberch's penalty kick in the Carabao Cup shootout against Liverpool at Anfield

The Vaseline tip has tended to be passed on from ‘keeper to ‘keeper. Ask Foster and he will say he learned it from Joe Hart. Ask Hart and he will credit Kasper Schmeichel. And so on.

For Johnsson, he believes there is a psychological benefit as it not only gave greater grip to his gloves but made him feel more confident in goal, particularly in wet weather.

Stamford Bridge was soaking when Penders struggled in his first Premier League start as Tottenham Hotspur visited Chelsea. That was a match played in the midst of Storm Boelo. At one corner, the youngster filling in for Emiliano Martinez mistimed a punch for an own goal. With that lead, Spurs went on to win 2-0, their first victory at the Bridge since 2018.

It is not known if Penders used the Vaseline hack in that derby defeat, but sources told Confidential to look out for his use of it in their following two fixtures versus Liverpool and United.

Penders put in a fine performance at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, despite Chelsea losing on penalties at Anfield after a 1-1 draw. Had Emmanuel Emegha scored his spot-kick, Xabi Alonso’s side would have reached the quarter-finals after Penders denied Ryan Gravenberch from 12 yards.

In Chelsea’s 2-0 Premier League victory over United, Penders made sure of his clean sheet with several saves, including a world-class stop as he tipped Bryan Mbeumo’s rocket on to his crossbar.

As mentioned, the hack is entirely legal. IFAB – football’s lawmakers – have no rule against Vaseline or any other petroleum jelly being applied to goalkeepers’ gloves in their regulations on player equipment.

Penders saves from Liverpool's Ronald Araujo during the Carabao Cup match

Penders punches a slippery ball into his own net against Tottenham on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge

In more goalkeeper news, Martinez has been privately pushing to play in Chelsea’s trip to Sunderland this Sunday, per sources who also revealed how he has been insisting to club colleagues that he wants to represent Argentina during the upcoming international break.

Since this information was relayed to Confidential earlier this week, Martinez has indeed been called up by Lionel Scaloni for his country’s friendlies versus Uruguay and Costa Rica. He is also understood to have returned to Chelsea training on Wednesday, albeit with strapping around his jaw.

Alonso confirmed at his last press conference that ‘there is a chance’ his goalkeeper could return before the break. That would leave Chelsea’s manager with a decision to make – whether to stick with Penders, who has shown his potential in the last two games, or turn to Martinez, who has seen a specialist while sidelined about having a face-mask fitted.

The 34-year-old broke his jaw in Chelsea’s 2-0 Premier League win away at Everton in mid-October. He had surgery, and said at the time that he would be ‘back in a few weeks’. That will be three weeks ago this weekend when Alonso’s squad travel to Sunderland.

Meanwhile, Aaron Anselmino has also been called up by Argentina, despite having not played a single minute for Chelsea this season. He has only made the match-day squad once as an unused substitute in their first game in the Carabao Cup against Luton Town in August.

Then he disappeared. But Confidential did spy Anselmino last Saturday for the first time in a while as he took a seat behind the bench, and now he is in Scaloni's squad. That is despite Alonso telling us at his last press conference that he was injured.

Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez breaks his jaw in a clash with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite last month

Marintez receives treatment on the Hill Dickinson Stadium turf - but is pushing for a return to action this weekend

SUNDERLAND WOULD PREFER PENDERS OVER MARTINEZ

Confidential asked former Sunderland striker Kevin Phillips whether he would rather face Penders or Martinez.

The 53-year-old, who scored 92 Premier League goals, told us: ‘The obvious one would be Penders, with his lack of experience, coming to the Stadium of Light, which is going to be a hostile, noisy occasion.

‘Emiliano, he's got the experience, played an awful long time at Villa. Obviously, he's had his injury, but he's an experienced international, been there, seen it and done it. So you would say Penders for his inexperience. But it looks like Martinez might be the one who starts, with a mask on, which, from Sunderland's point of view, means you're going to have to test him.’

Phillips spoke to us via Best Betting Sites and when asked if Martinez’s recent injury would impact Sunderland’s approach if he is in goal, he said: ‘The natural one with Martinez is that nobody wants to go and hurt him again. It's a terrible injury, so you don't want a recurrence.

‘So anything physical, no. But from a wide point of view, getting the ball in the box, from set-plays, put the ball in high, just to see if he's confident to come for crosses, come and punch it. That would be my advice, certainly not to get physical with him.

‘Take every opportunity to shoot. Put him under pressure early and see how he copes. But from Chelsea's point of view, if he wasn't 100 per cent, they wouldn't risk him.’

Chelsea sources who were consulted by Confidential after Estevao was suddenly handed his first Premier League start of the season have explained why Manchester United were deliberately picked as the opponents.

We are told Alonso has had concerns about the 19-year-old Brazilian’s physicality and Chelsea’s fitness staff have been tasked with working on building him up. But United, managed by Michael Carrick, were seen as ideal opposition for him to face from the beginning.

United were considered weaker than the Premier League's other physical sides, which lessened Alonso’s reservations. Estevao did indeed have fun, could not be tamed by Diogo Dalot, and was unfortunate not to get among the goals in the 2-0 win.

It remains to be seen if Estevao will now keep his place away at Sunderland, where Chelsea crumbled on the final day of last season to end up out of Europe.

Estevao (left) was given a rare start against Manchester United at the weekend when he teamed up nicely with Morgan Rogers

There were some interesting quotes from Regis Le Bris last week as the Sunderland boss praised his centre back Omar Alderete after they beat Brentford in the Carabao Cup.

'We spoke about the style of play,’ Le Bris said. ‘We try to press high. It’s more or less the trend of the Premier League. You press up, and it means your opponent will go long. If your centre backs are not strong, consistent and able to manage one v ones, it’s over. Thank you, Omar.’

Except, Alderete is now suspended for the visit of Chelsea, and despite Le Bris liking to press high, the statistics say only Coventry have won possession in the final third fewer times than Sunderland this season.

It is a big game for Le Bris, who has avoided losing his job while his side sit bottom of the Premier League with a vote of confidence coming from his board in the build-up to Chelsea’s visit.

This weekend's Chelsea match is a big one for Regis Le Bris, the under-pressure Sunderland manager

Chelsea are making significant money on having fans lay out their favourite player’s kit and boots in the changing room on a matchday, while the supporter can also leave a good-luck message.

The ‘VVIP dressing room experience’ is already a sell-out for Chelsea’s next Premier League home game versus Leeds United on Saturday, November 21 at £750 per person.

There are other perks which come with that package – you aren’t just paying to do the kit-man’s job for him – but it is another example of Chelsea’s outside-of-the-box hospitality ideas.

#1293. Fleetwood knock out Arsenal in one of biggest shocks in League Cup history

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

“You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”

This was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and said “stop”.

A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM

The precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury.

So while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed.

The anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

Arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”

They were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

It was a League Two goal in its simplicity, but that is no criticism. Harrison Neal helped a long ball forward, putting it behind Marli Salmon and Aaron Loupalo-Bi relished the chance to get into a foot race, grappling with the England Under-17 international.

Salmon looked like he had him at one point, but Loupalo-Bi was strong – not to mention composed – and he held off the challenge to slide a left-footed shot through the legs of Illan Meslier, who was making his Arsenal debut. What followed was unique to the magic of an English cup tie.

FLEETWOOD TAKE THE LEAD! 😱 Loupalo-Bi puts League Two side Fleetwood ahead against Arsenal 💥 https://t.co/zTFEkCp0oL

As the home fans set off flares, filling the air with plumes of thick, red smoke, the theme tune to Captain Pugwash was played. Arteta tried to find answers from his coaching staff, amid the cacophony, but occasionally you do not have to look too deep for answers.

Could the miracle happen? When half-time arrived with Fleetwood still in the lead, you began to wonder. But then you saw Ben White and Martin Odegaard go through intense warm-ups so they could be introduced at the start of the second half and you knew the mountain had become taller.

So it proved. Odegaard, with his mesmerising left foot and all-encompassing vision, did more in the first five minutes of the second period than many of his colleagues had managed before the interval, and Arsenal levelled in that initial flurry through Gyökeres’s first domestic goal of the campaign.

Viktor Gyökeres gets his first goal of the season and Arsenal are level against Fleetwood! 🔴 https://t.co/LfZcIbAfCX

A game of attack against defence played out for the remainder before Dowman was harshly dismissed in the 85th minute after reacting to a tough challenge from Neal. There was still time for Fleetwood’s Lynch to make two excellent saves from White and Odegaard in added time as Arsenal tried to avoid the shoot-out lottery. They could not and how it hurt them.

HUGE save from Jay Lynch! https://t.co/dLJaFwCmHQ

“Football’s getting a little bit more, I don’t know, clinical and removed,” Matt Lawlor, the Fleetwood manager, said. “To me, there was that feeling we all get as football fans. That was what you kind of live for, isn’t it? To be a part of it is special.

“To be giving that to football fans and especially Fleetwood fans is unbelievably special. I’m really proud of it. Football’s a funny old game, isn’t it?”

First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through in the next round, in the manner they’ve done it, the atmosphere they have created, and, yeah, a really sad day for us.

I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players. I haven’t seen anyone not doing what is required at this level. But, obviously, we insisted so much, we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, obviously, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn’t. And football is about that.

Attitude wise, absolutely zero [wrong] otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way. It had nothing to do with effort or application or determination to win it, but we lack other things to, to create a much bigger margin than today, with what we produce, they really should have been shown in the scoreline.

Something that we discussed already before the match.

It’s difficult to see on the cameras, I prefer to watch it back properly and I will assess the situation.

We will learn from everything [on if he will learn from it].

I don’t think it will [sink in], it’s really hard to address the players when we have a league game on Saturday and I didn’t want to be the bearer of reality. The biggest night in the club’s history. We’ve beaten the champions, somehow!

We knew before the game, we’re not stupid enough and not egotistical enough that you think we’re going to go to the best team in the country and the most organised team in the country and the best of the basics and the world-class players, in that we’re going to go and outplay them. So we had to ride our luck, we had to deny space, we had to deny options for them. And I think we did that really, really well in terms of the majority of the game.

Obviously, the goal happens, but they’re going to happen; they’re so good at football. The footballers that they have, the gaps that they find and we see it every week in the Premier League.

To beat the English champions on penalties, credit to everyone one of these lads. We looked at Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We compared it even though these are the champions. We thought ‘if we lay it all out there, let’s see what happens.

The team who are 18th in League Two have beaten the Premier League champions. Nine perfect penalties and one miss from Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal making another couple of changes: Guimaraes and Konsa replace Lewis-Skelly and Zubimendi.

For Fleetwood: Davies replaces Loupalo-Bi.

Ben White caught offside just as Arsenal were building up a head of steam in attack. “Champion of England, you’re having a laugh” is the chant from the home fans.

From that Arsenal free-kick, Havertz’s low cross goes straight into the side-netting. The German has had a bit of a stinker, Arsenal will need better at Anfield on Sunday. I’m sure Arteta would have liked to have taken off Havertz or Gyokeres by now.

Haughey wins an important tackle on Lewis-Skelly after Arsenal found the free player in the box, and from the resulting short corner Dowman’s shot is straight Lynch.

Dowman is then hacked down by Batty, who was tempted in by a heavy touch. Booking for the Fleetwood defender.

If the game finishes level, we will go straight to penalties. One or two players on both teams with heavy legs, but Arsenal surely have to turn the screw from here.

Coughlan is an in-form striker who is trying to offer Fleetwood some more intensity and pressing from the front. Despite all that Arsenal pressure, Fleetwood have not gone under since conceding the equaliser.

Havertz hesitant after Odegaard picked out his run and split the Fleetwood defence again. Neither let fly with the shot from a tight angle, nor picked out a cutback. Two changes from Fleetwood: Evans and McClean off, Coughlan and Murphy on.

And a change from Arsenal: O’Neill off, replaced by Eze. O’Neill was one of Arsenal’s brighter starters.

Bodies on the line from Fleetwood to keep the scores level, first Havertz and then Lewis Skelly had shots blocked from a free-kick floated into the box. Fleetwood need to hope for a second wind from somewhere.

Odegaard with another delightful flicked pass, but Havertz could only poke the ball into the side netting. Should be doing better with that chance, he had half of the goal to aim at. Arsenal knocking on the door, feels like a second goal is coming.

As you would expect, Fleetwood now finding it very difficult to get out of their half or establish any possession. They will not be hanging this one in the National Gallery, but Arsenal are level. Bright play from O’Neill down the left, putting his marker on his heels and whipping early delivery into the box. Gyokeres needed a couple of stabs at it, but the application of studs on ball was enough to sneak it beyond the goalkeeper.

Martin Odegaard has done more in five minutes than any of the 11 who were on the pitch in the first half. A class act, the best midfielder in the Premier League when he is on song.

No messing around here from Arsenal. Martin Odegaard and Ben White have both done a rigorous half-time warm up and will be introduced immediately.

Odegaard and White on, replacing Timber and Salmon. I think that means Lewis-Skelly to left-back.

Arsenal waste a corner just before half-time whistle, and they have 45 minutes to spare themselves an embarrassing League Cup exit to League Two Fleetwood Town. The home team scored with their only shot of the game, with Arsenal’s defence undone a little too easily and Marli Salmon exposed.

More menace about Arsenal’s last few attacks, with Lewis-Skelly and Havertz combining and then Bennett doing ever so well to clear Dowman’s driven cross. Havertz then skews a header wide, from another Dowman delivery.

Gyokeres with a snap shot that he was always stretching for and it was simple work for the goalkeeper Lynch. Half hour gone, but we will be playing until almost 55 minutes in this first half.

Hincapie’s pass towards O’Neill goes astray. Fleetwood’s defensive shape is serving them well so far, they are defending in a 5-4-1 are limiting space. When Arsenal do lose the ball, they look open. They needed a Zubimendi interception to thwart a counter-attack after a Mosquera givaway.

Max Dowman runs out of room down the right as some rain swirls around the stadium. I’m not sure there will be any panic in the Arsenal ranks, but they need to be crisper than they have been so far.

Something of a scramble from a wide Arsenal free-kick but the home team survive and there is a huge roar from the home crowd. Lewis-Skelly then slips in midfield and Loupalo-Bi helps drag Fleetwood up the pitch.

One of the two Fleetwood players to come into the team from the defeat by Exeter has scored, Loupalo-Bi. He pinned Salmon as the last man and rolled the young Arsenal defender, before poking the ball through the legs of Meslier. Loupalo-Bi is on loan from Fulham. Is the shock of all shocks on?

Well, well, well. The stadium reeks of sulphur from the red plumes of smoke that have been set off in celebration. Whatever criticisms you have of English football, a night like this when the minnows serve it up to giants is exactly what makes the sport great. Fleetwood might not hold on but, goodness, they have given the locals something to enjoy.

First big chance of the game falls to Arsenal. Salmon’s pass forward deflected through to Dowman, but he scuffed the ball across goal with his right foot just in front of Gyokeres. Could he have run around the ball and curled the shot with his left? He looked to have had the time.

Arsenal starting to apply some pressure now, and the attacks are coming from their right flank through Timber and Dowman. Rooney wins a crunching 50:50 at the edge of the box to deny Lewis-Skelly a clear shot on goal. Great block.

Another throw-in for Fleetwood high up the pitch, won by Ched Evans. Fleetwood need all of the levellers they can get tonight, and you wonder if that long stoppage right from the off can be one.

The Highbury Chippy has been doing a roaring trade and plenty of customers from north London enjoyed the chance to wallow in some nostalgia. One man who isn’t interested in sentiment is Mikel Arteta and the strength of the team he has named indicates how serious he is about going all the way in this competition. Max Dowman is going to be in everyone’s gaze but this is an important night for Viktor Gyokeres, who has a chance to build up his confidence after a disappointing start to the campaign.

The Arsenal midfielder suffered a broken nose just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute against Everton.

We made two changes, one enforced through suspension. We had to make changes because we have a packed schedule and we have the champions coming to town and there’s a way we want to go and play.

The steepest from winning the league last year. It will be a very difficult challenge we have to come up against. They have paid a lot of respect to the competition and us by naming such a strong team. We understand it’s a difficult challenge.

It’s always very special, this competition and coming to these kinds of grounds, it’s proper English football. We’re very excited about it and we’re going to take it seriously.

It’s great to have Marli, Max and Ceadach with us, and Illan as well, who since he’s joined, hasn’t had the opportunity to start a game. We always say everybody’s going to be important, they need to feel like it, and the only way to do that is to play minutes.

For sure, because that’s the best way to express yourself, when you have the chance and you have to play. Give me a headache, give me a problem, and give me reasons to play more. So far, the boys have done that very well.

A curious quirk of their modern history is that Arsenal have won eight of their last nine FA Cup finals – Liverpool in 2001 their one defeat – but have lost four League Cup finals in a row since they last won the competition in 1993.

Arsène Wenger used the competition to blood younger players, and that remains the case for Arsenal despite them carrying a bigger, more experienced squad nowadays.

Nevertheless, given the impressive record of Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool and Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City in the League Cup, it is an itch Arteta will want to scratch.

Arteta’s Arsenal have not won a major final in front of fans, and they are too good a side to allow that state of affairs to drag on.

Did he pick up a knock against Everton or has he been rested? I suspect it could be the former, because he was a candidate to start and give either Havertz or Odeegaard the night off.

Aaron Loupalo-Bi comes into the team from the weekend’s defeat at Exeter City. Ched Evans is their centre-forward.

Fleetwood Town XI: Lynch, Rooney, Haughey, Potter, Neal, Bennett, McLean, Helm, Batty, Evans, Loupalo-Bi

Subs: Pradic, Andrew, Cannon, Davies, Thomas, Murphy, Coughlan, Robertson, Cirino

They are the three youngsters in Mikel Arteta’s team. It’s a debut for Ceadach O’Neill. Timber, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz are the three starters who could start at Anfield, so I would not expect 90 minutes from any of them. Raya, Gabriel, Calafiori and Rice the first-teamers given the night off. So too Noni Madueke, which speaks to his rising status within the squad.

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡 Your Carabao Cup Gunners 👊 🤝 @deel

Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Eberechi Eze are among the players stepping off the bus, so at the very least it will be a strong bench.

Aside from their stadium being called Highbury, Fleetwood Town’s red shirts with white sleeves also bear a striking resemblance to Arsenal’s home kit. The club in its current guise was founded in 1997, although previous iterations date back to 1908 under the name Fleetwood FC.

There is no evidence or anecdote suggesting Arsenal were the inspiration, so it appears the kit clash is a coincidence. Arsenal will be wearing their navy away strip.

The club’s most famous son is surely Jamie Vardy, who scored 31 goals in 36 appearances for Fleetwood in the 2011-12 season before Leicester City made their move.

An unfamiliar opponent at a very familiar sounding venue, Arsenal play Fleetwood Town for the first time this evening at the Lancashire club’s Highbury Stadium.

Fleetwood, 18th in League Two, are the lowest-ranked team remaining in this season’s League Cup, having booked their place in the fourth round thanks to a victory at Sheffield United.

They were playing in English football’s sixth tier in 2009, and so while their stadium may share its name with Arsenal’s former home, the two clubs are worlds apart.

The League Cup is fourth of four competitions on Arsenal’s list of priorities, but Mikel Arteta should be able to rotate extensively while progressing to the quarter-finals. With a trip to Anfield on Sunday, that is a welcome luxury.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres are seasoned internationals in need of minutes and in line to start.

Max Dowman lit up Arsenal’s third-round victory at Ipswich Town, and 17-year-old centre-back Marli Salmon was not far behind him. Young striker and Northern Ireland international Ceadach O’Neill is also expected to be involved, and he may be joined by other academy players.

While attention is fixed on Premier League and Champions League success, Arsenal’s stinging defeat by Manchester City in last season’s final of this competition will not have been forgotten by Arteta or his players.

Matt Lawlor, Fleetwood’s manager, was full of praise for Arsenal in his pre-match press conference: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch. The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.

“We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”

Arteta has told his players that they must keep their standards high, with a lack of concentration or professionalism potentially their worst enemy against fourth-tier opposition.

Arteta said: “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.“We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that’s why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game.”Full team news on the way shortly.

Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi is reportedly a transfer target for Atletico Madrid, who are also eyeing up Manchester United centre-back Lisandro Martinez.

The Spanish giants are said to be leading the race to sign Zubimendi, who has fallen down the pecking order at Arsenal in recent times despite initially making a strong start to life at the Emirates Stadium last season.

The 27-year-old impressed at Real Sociedad and immediately looked at home at Arsenal, forming a strong partnership with Declan Rice and proving a key figure for Mikel Arteta’s side as they ended their 22-year wait to win the Premier League title.

Still, Zubimendi lost his place towards the end of the campaign and has barely featured so far this term, with talkSPORT now linking him strongly with Atletico Madrid.

They claim Diego Simeone has approved the move, though the Spain international has also been linked strongly with Chelsea by the Independent.

We recently covered Zubimendi’s situation here, with the understanding being that Arsenal would prefer to keep him for the rest of this season at least.

Still, things can change, and it is clear that the former Sociedad man has struggled to impress for a while now, with more competition for places since Bruno Guimaraes’ arrival in the summer.

Zubimendi will surely not want to spend that much longer warming the bench, but it remains to be seen if AFC will be prepared to sanction an exit when they need the squad depth.

All in all, it’s an intriguing situation that seems worth keeping an eye on, with top clubs likely to be interested in a quality player like this if he does become available.

Another Atletico target mentioned by talkSPORT is Man Utd defender Martinez, who seems more likely to definitely be on the move soon.

The Argentina international has struggled to reach his best form at Old Trafford and he’s also put himself in a difficult position after his recent public outburst against sporting director Jason Wilcox.

Atletico would surely do very well to land two proven talents like this in one go.

#1291. These AI agents design your perfect robot-powered lab — and run it for you

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Artificial-intelligence agents can devise a detailed procedure for a robotic arm and test it in a virtual laboratory.Credit: Jiaru Bai & Yuchi Zhao, University of Toronto

Laboratory robots are tireless and uncomplaining, but they have narrow skill sets, limited mobility and an inability to get out of each other’s way. Now, a system of artificial-intelligence agents promises to help lab robots do their best work.

In this process, a scientist describes their research programme and lab set-up to the agents, which then create step-by-step experimental protocols for the lab’s robots. The agents also generate a virtual version of the lab and test the protocols there. They can then direct the robots in the real lab to perform the research.

Robot chemist sparks row with claim it created new materials

Robot chemist sparks row with claim it created new materials

The agents can even design an entire lab from scratch, using a virtual one to work out the ideal placement for instruments and robots.

The system is described in a preprint posted in October to arXiv1. It has not been peer reviewed.

In a test, the agents wrote more than 200 commands directing a robotic arm to move between and interact with instruments in an existing lab space. The agent simulated the steps in the virtual lab to ensure that it all worked smoothly, then directed the real-life arm to carry out procedures to measure the optical properties of nanocrystals.

The concept is “very cool” and could drastically reduce the effort required to set up automated labs, says Evan Collins, a bioengineer at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge. But integrating the cameras and sensors that the agents need to direct experiments effectively could require more resources than does setting up a lab manually, he says.

The simulations would make it easy to plan robotic movements that avoid collisions between robots and other objects in the lab, says Collins.

This could ease the process of getting labs up and running, given that setting up an automated lab is often a time-consuming process of trial and error followed by extensive testing and troubleshooting. Because the agents conduct all the planning and testing in a simulated environment, there is no need for researchers to “babysit the system” after it’s built, says Yuchi (Allan) Zhao, a roboticist at the University of Toronto in Canada and co-author of the preprint.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03587-x

Bai, J. et al. Preprint at arXiv https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.23826 (2026).

Manchester United are reportedly eyeing up a potential transfer move for Brentford centre-back Nathan Collins for January after failing to strengthen in that position in the summer.

It’s been a terrible start to the season for Man Utd, who drew 4-4 with Aston Villa in their most recent game, which could finally spell the end for manager Michael Carrick.

Still, the manager is not the only problem at Old Trafford, with some questionable decisions made over the summer when the club only signed three new midfielders and failed to fix other areas of their squad.

MORE: Proof Brentford are one of the best-run clubs in the Premier League and Man United are the worst

According to the Daily Mail, this ‘costly misjudgement’ could now see the Red Devils move for Brentford’s Collins this winter, while Fulham’s Calvin Bassey is also mentioned as an option under consideration.

We’ve often seen Brentford selling star names to bigger clubs, with Bryan Mbeumo a recent example as he also left the Bees to join United.

It could be that Collins will be their next major sale, with the Republic of Ireland international often impressing as one of their most solid performers at the back.

Earlier this year, United were linked with Collins by TEAMtalk, while the likes of Liverpool and Tottenham have also been mentioned as suitors by Football Insider.

It certainly seems inevitable that Brentford are going to struggle to keep Collins, and one imagines plenty of MUFC fans would be happy to see him join in the near future as an upgrade on the out-of-form Lisandro Martinez, and the ageing Harry Maguire.
