#1267. Preprint platform offers to pay researchers to review papers, but questions remain

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Paying researchers to review papers is seen as a potential solution to clearing the peer-reviewing backlog.Credit: UpPiJ/iStock via Getty

A preprint platform is paying researchers for reviewing preprints uploaded by other scientists, reigniting debates about whether peer reviewers should be paid.

XSci, which launched in September, will reward a reviewer with US$200 if they send their feedback within five days of accepting the task and $100 if they do so between five and ten days. The fee is covered by other researchers, who pay XSci to have their preprints reviewed by scholars. The preprint website, which does not publish a journal, charges each author $399 for a round of review or $249 if they make their review report public.

The system enables authors to receive comments quickly while compensating reviewers for their time and effort, says Shumiao Ouyang, the founder of XSci, the start-up firm incorporated in Delaware that runs the platform. The company has received around $500,000 from private investors and is trying to raise more funds, Ouyang says.

A publishing platform that places code front and centre

A publishing platform that places code front and centre

“What authors get is an answer, usually within about five to ten days, to the question they care about most: does this paper have a real chance at the journals I am aiming at? Today, that answer can take months, and in some fields, years,” says Ouyang, who is an economist at the University of Oxford, UK. XSci also charges authors up to $19 to have their preprints reviewed by a range of artificial-intelligence programs, although access to some AI tools is free.

Several researchers interviewed by Nature say that XSci’s business model is interesting, but that its future will depend mostly on whether it can attract authors to use its human-reviewing service.

“Will authors be willing to pay such a fee? Where does the money come from?” asks developmental biologist and toxicologist Daniel Gorelick at Baylor College of Medicine in Houston, Texas, who has served as editor-in-chief of Biology Open since July 2023.

But Gorelick also says that cash payments are “a powerful incentive”. Biology Open, an open-access journal published by The Company of Biologists, has been paying reviewers £220 (or $280) per manuscript since 2024 through a programme called Fast and Fair. The payment is issued to the reviewer if they send in their work on time and if its quality meets the editors’ expectations.

Ouyang expects XSci’s core authors to be doctoral and postdoctoral students, as well as early-career researchers “who often cannot wait for a year or more for a journal’s decision”.

Peer reviewers are conventionally expected to review manuscripts as a service to the scientific community, rather than for a fee. By paying them at the preprint stage, Ouyang says, XSci intends to tackle challenges that dog the academic publishing industry today: how to convince scholars to review the work of others and to do it quickly.

Several studies1–3 have shown that journal editors are finding it increasingly difficult to source reviewers for various reasons, including a rising number of submissions and academics’ growing workloads. These and other issues often lead to a long review time, which can range from a few weeks to several months.

XSci states on its website that academics can register their interest to be paid reviewers. But in reality, says Ouyang, a scholar must be invited by the website to review a manuscript. The website nevertheless has a ‘register interest’ field for practical reasons because, he explains, “it tells us how many willing researchers there are in each field.”

Shumiao Ouyang is an economist at the University of Oxford, UK, and founder of XSci.Credit: Yizhen Zhang

Ouyang says that XSci has developed an AI program to help find suitable reviewers quickly. Once an author uploads their manuscript to XSci and chooses the human-reviewing option, the AI tool will compile a ranking of potential reviewers by screening candidates from three sources: the scientists who wrote the papers that the manuscript cites, those scholars’ regular collaborators and researchers who have published papers on similar topics in the author’s target journals. The AI program will rank, then e-mail, potential reviewers one by one. Each potential reviewer has 12 hours to accept the job, says Ouyang.

If the reviewer thinks that the manuscript could be published in the author’s target journals after reasonable changes, the preprint will be given a badge on the website, demonstrating that it has been reviewed and is endorsed by the reviewer.

In time, XSci hopes to form partnerships with journal publishers that would allow the journals’ editors to use XSci’s review reports as part of their assessments. This would happen only if the authors and reviewers both agree to the reports being shared, Ouyang says. The idea is that editors can decide what to do with XSci’s reviews: whether to use them to replace one round of their own reviews or as external references, he adds. In follow-up questions from Nature, however, Ouyang stressed that the badge would merely “become useful information for an editor”.

“Whether a journal gives them any weight is the entirely the journal’s decision,” he added.

In 2025, Fast and Fair helped to slash the time that Biology Open editors spent making the first decision about a manuscript from an average of 37.7 working days under the free-reviewing route to an average of 5.5 working days, according to a preprint co-authored by Gorelick4. The programme also led to review invitations having a higher acceptance rate and a higher completion rate of accepted tasks, the study found.

But a separate study found that paying reviewers did not achieve substantial improvements. Editors at Critical Care Medicine, a journal published by Lippincott Williams & Wilkins, carried out a six-month experiment in which they sent reviewers invitations with or without monetary incentives in alternating two-week blocks5. They found that 50% of review invitations with a $250 cash reward resulted in a peer-review report in 14 days, compared with 42% of invitations without the fee. Paid reviewers also delivered their work just one day quicker on average than did non-paid reviewers.

“It didn’t move the needle too much,” says David Maslove, one of the editors who co-authored in the study and a clinician-scientist at Queen’s University in Kingston, Canada.

‘Getting paid to review is justice’: journal pays peer reviewers in cryptocurrency

‘Getting paid to review is justice’: journal pays peer reviewers in cryptocurrency

A paying system comes with challenges, researchers warn. There need to be stringent quality controls, as well as policies in place to ensure that reviewers don’t game the system and publishers don’t take advantage of reviewers, Gorelick says. “You can’t just pay reviewers and walk away,” he notes.

“XSci currently does not check the quality of the reviews done by the reviewers before they are released to the authors,” says Jeffery Poon, publishing and editorial lead of XSci. If the authors are not satisfied with what they receive, they can initiate an appeal through XSci, Poon notes. XSci plans to provide tools to reviewers to help them check their own work, but the team is still working out how that could be implemented in reality, he adds.

#1266. Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City

This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. #1265. He Played 464 Games For Man Utd - But Depression Ruined His England Career

For many English football players, playing for the senior England national team is the pinnacle of your career.

Current captain Harry Kane is expected to become the most capped player of all-time when England take on Croatia on Thursday night at Wembley, where he will earn his 126th cap, surpassing Peter Shilton's 125 appearances for the Three Lions.

Just behind them is former captain and former all-time top scorer Wayne Rooney, who earned 121 caps in his senior career, who enjoyed a stunning individual career at club level during his time at Everton, Manchester United, and DC United.

While playing at Old Trafford in particular, Rooney played alongside a host of world-class talent, many of whom were English. Gary Neville, Rio Ferdinand, Owen Hargreaves, and Paul Scholes all enjoyed brilliant careers at international level as well as with United, and they all absolutely loved their time with the Three Lions.

But someone else who played with those stars and represented the national team wasn't so keen, and has admitted that he was actually depressed during that time of his career.

Iconic midfielder Michael Carrick was considered to be one of the most underrated midfielders of his generation, because he barely got the nod at international level.

Carrick won 34 caps during his career, never scoring a goal, with just 22 of those appearances coming as a starter. But only 12 of those 34 appearances came in competitive games, with the rest coming in friendlies, showing that the managers rarely relied on him when it really mattered.

But speaking back in 2018, while still a player, Carrick revealed that part of the reason why he never earned more caps was because he asked for the FA to stop picking him as he felt depressed whenever he went away for camps.

“I’d been in the squad a long time and I’ll be honest, I was finding it hard going away with England. I didn’t mind going away with United pre-season for three weeks or whatever and coming back, but going with England, it was almost depressing in a way," he said.

“It made me really down, so I came to the point after South Africa where I thought: ‘I can’t do that again.’ People would be saying: ‘Pull yourself together and be grateful for it’ and I understood the position I was in, the privileged position I was in, but I just found it so hard, and I couldn’t deal with it anymore.

“I was probably on the verge of ... yes, I was depressed at times, yes. I told the FA: ‘Look, please don’t pick me.’”

Carrick was part of the England squad at the 2006 and 2010 World Cups, while he was on standby for the 2014 World Cup too. But he made just one appearance in a tournament, where he started in the 1-0 win over Ecuador in Stuttgart.

England's lack of success at tournaments was often put down to the failed partnership of Steven Gerrard and Frank Lampard in the centre of midfield, and with Carrick's reveal that he asked to be left out towards the end of his career, whether he could have been the difference maker will always remain one of the greatest what-ifs of that generation.

#1264. HMRC chase the estate of late ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson for £3.5MILLION in unpaid tax - because he was 'too busy with his ladies to save'

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:19 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 06:25 EST, 10 November 2026

Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) for an outstanding £3.5million in tax owed.

It comes as a result of the estate's inheritance following Eriksson's death in August 2024 due to pancreatic cancer.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last year, the former England manager reportedly had assets worth £4.8m but owed a staggering £7.25m to HMRC alone. He also reportedly had at least £1m outstanding in other debts.

In a bid to help reduce that outstanding debt, his family sold his old mansion called Bjorkefors last year - albeit at a substantial loss.

Eriksson is survived by his son Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39 - from his first marriage to Ann-Christine Pettersson - as well as partner Yaniseth Alcides. During his time as England manager he had a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio.

Speaking to The Sun, Eriksson's lawyer Anders Runebjer has revealed that the estate has no money left to settle the debt - aside from £300,000 in a UK bank and £1m in a Cayman Islands tax haven. He also stated his focus is now to salvage any money for Eriksson's two children after the ex-Three Lions boss had spent his finances around football and women.

Ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased for £3.5million by HMRC

In August 2024, he passed away at the age of 76 following a battle with pancreatic cancer

The Swede is survived by his two children Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39

'Sven earned millions but was always too busy with his football and his ladies to manage money very well,' said Runebjer.

'I told the HMRC I'm not able to get the money in the Cayman Islands or his UK bank and said they're welcome to seize it.

'They replied that they couldn't do that so I told them there was nothing else left - so they won't get paid.

'Sven was regularly sent bills by the British taxman and paid promptly but they changed the rules and now say he still owes £3.5m plus interest after he passed away.

'They're welcome to take whatever they can get but I'm not giving them anything.

'My priority is trying to get whatever money I can that he left for his children - not the British taxman.'

As aforementioned, Eriksson's estate sold his seven-bed house in Torsby, in his native Sweden - located on the banks of Lake Fryken - but at a reduced price.

According to The Sun, the property was on the market for £2m but his family had to lower the price by £400,000 to attract any prospective buyers.

And they went on to add that an anonymous e-commerce businesswoman has now bought it for an undisclosed sum of at least £1.3m - meaning a potential £700,000 loss on market value alone. However, the loss is greater as Eriksson bought the place in 2002 for £4.5m - meaning the true value lost is around £3m.

Last year, Eriksson's former home in Sweden was sold as his family look to reduce debt

Eriksson lived in the property with his partner Yaniseth Alcides until his death

During his time as England boss, he was in a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio

Selling the property was the latest thing Eriksson's family have done in a bid to ease the financial burden they have taken on since his death.

In March 2025, they were forced to auction off his memorabilia - such as a lunch invitation from the late Queen.

Also up for auction was his Armani suit from a 2006 World Cup match with his hand-written team notes still in the pocket.

The 349 items reported to have gone under the hammer for a combined total of £140,000 also include his BBC Coach of the Year trophy in 2001 and a Premier League Manager of the Month award from his time as Manchester City boss.

An Ivory Coast top signed with a special message by former forward Didier Drogba from Eriksson's time as national coach in 2010 was sold as well.

Eriksson was estimated to have received around £7m in pay-offs alone from England, Manchester City and Mexico during his managerial career.

The Swede, who managed England between 2001 and 2006, previously described himself as being 'stupid' with his money.

In one of his last ever interviews, he told The Guardian: 'I was never interested in money - I never took care of it and trusted people to do that for me. I was stupid not to control where the money went. I realised that when I didn't have any more cash!

'I still don't know what I have in the bank.'

#1263. 2026/27 Premier League Table Without 'VAR Errors'

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018.  He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

Video Assistant Referee (VAR) has its fair share of critics. Introduced to the Premier League at the start of the 2019/20 season, the technology was designed to help the on-pitch officials and ensure matches were officiated seamlessly and without controversy.

However, it has not had the impact that it was intended to have. If anything, the number of refereeing controversies has gone up, and many high-profile names, including Roy Keane and Wayne Rooney, have lost patience and want to see VAR scrapped.

But what would the 2026/27 Premier League table look like if every refereeing decision was correct? After every matchday in England's top tier, Squawka asks their followers to vote on controversial VAR decisions and whether the right decision was made or not.

Using that data, they have created a Premier League table without VAR errors following matchday 10, and it makes for interesting reading.

The table has been compiled on the basis that penalties, should they have been awarded, would have been converted.

Sunderland have had a dismal start to the campaign. The Black Cats, who are competing in the Conference League after finishing seventh in 2025/26, are currently rock bottom of the Premier League, having picked up five points from their opening ten games. They can't blame VAR for their troubles, either, as they would remain in the same position without its errors.

Crystal Palace would be second bottom, with Manchester United rounding out the relegation places. Nottingham Forest, who are currently 16th in the Premier League, would be two points better off and would be up in 14th, above Palace and United in the table, had VAR been perfect.

Back in September, Forest and Tottenham Hotspur drew 0-0 at the City Ground. VAR is adjudged to have wrongly intervened to disallow Neco Williams' goal for the home side. The Premier League released a statement explaining the goal had been ruled out for handball, but many felt the footage was inconclusive and not clear and obvious. Had VAR made the right decision, Forest would have won 1-0.

Coventry City currently sit 17th in the table, as is correct for them. But Fulham actually find themselves one place higher than they should be, as a result of Forest's issues.

Hull City have had a tremendous start and currently sit 13th in the table, but they would be a point and two places worse off without VAR errors.

Tottenham Hotspur would find themselves two places worse off down in 13th if VAR decisions were correct, while Ipswich Town would be two places and two points better off up in 12th. Newcastle United currently find themselves in 12th in the table, but the Magpies would be up in 11th with an extra point and a +6 goal difference swing in their favour.

Premier League Table Without VAR Errors (20-11)

Aston Villa are currently the team propping up the top half of the table with 13 points and a -3 goal difference from their opening ten games. But while their league position wouldn't have changed, the VAR decisions being correct would have them two points better off.

Leeds have had a strong start to the season, but they would be one point worse off in ninth in the table without any VAR errors, while Bournemouth would be dropping down to 8th in the table, with a -1 swing in their goal difference.

Everton would find themselves in 7th in the table, one place worse off, although they would still have 16 points and a +2 goal difference. Brentford are the biggest losers in the top half of the table, as they would be two places better off up in 6th place with two more points.

While the top five would be unchanged in terms of their standings, the points totals would be widely different. Chelsea and Liverpool currently sit fifth and fourth in the Premier League table with 16 and 18 points respectively, but with VAR errors being corrected, both teams should be on 19 points.

Manchester City would be two points worse off in third place, also on 19 points if VAR errors were fixed. They won 1-0 at Old Trafford thanks to Erling Haaland's winner. ProRef released a statement revealing that the goal should have been ruled out due to Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position. Without that goal, the match would've ended in a goalless draw.

Brighton would still be second place on 22 points with a +19 goal difference, but they should be two points closer to league leaders Arsenal.

Arsenal have picked up 27 points from their opening nine matches, winning nine and losing one. They wouldn't have beaten Liverpool without VAR errors, though.

Liverpool felt aggrieved that they weren't given a penalty when Alexander Isak's shirt was tugged by Jurrien Timber in the box, preventing him from having a header at goal. If VAR had made the right decision, Liverpool would've been given a spot-kick, and it is assumed they would have scored and that the spoils would have been shared.

Despite that, Mikel Arteta's side would still be well clear at the top of the table without VAR errors.

Premier League Table Without VAR Errors (10-1)

#1259. Man Utd: Moises Caicedo Slammed Mauricio Pochettino’s Tactics

Manchester United are currently finalising a deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager to replace Michael Carrick, GIVEMESPORT understands.

The Red Devils have had a disappointing season so far, sitting 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening ten games, which has led the club to make the decision that a change is necessary.

Pochettino, who is currently in charge of the USMNT, has a £7.4m exit clause in his contract with US Soccer, and GMS understands that it will cost a further £1.5m for him to bring his backroom staff with him too. But a deal is now close to being finalised, with Carrick expected to be relieved of his duties in the coming days.

Pochettino has previously had spells at three different Premier League clubs, having shone during a spell with Southampton, before taking over at Tottenham Hotspur and leading them to a second-place finish in the top flight, while he also reached the EFL Cup final and Champions League final with the north London side.

A brief spell with Paris Saint-Germain followed, where he won the Ligue 1 title, before he returned to London to coach Chelsea. At Stamford Bridge, he led the team to a fourth-place finish while he also reached the EFL Cup final again, losing in extra-time to Liverpool.

But despite a relatively successful season with the Blues, Pochettino was sacked after just one season with the club.

Pochettino's time at Chelsea is best remembered for the form and performances of Cole Palmer under his management, and Man Utd fans will be hopeful that he can get similar performances out of a number of stars at Old Trafford.

The poor campaign this season has been well noted, and many have blamed the poor running stats of Carrick's team. United have ranked second bottom of the entire division for distance covered and distance covered per 90 minutes, behind only Liverpool.

During pre-season, new midfield signing Youri Tielemans revealed that there wasn't a lot of running being done in pre-season, which attracted a lot of attention.

"That's [ball work] what it's been like mostly," he said on Rio Ferdinand Presents.

"Not loads of running?" Ferdinand queried.

"When you come back from the World Cup, you don't do loads of running. Just chill."

But speaking after Pochettino's exit at Chelsea, midfield general Moises Caicedo commented on the tactics he would employ, and noted that they relied heavily on running and fitness to be successful.

"At Brighton, it was all tactical, just with the ball; tactical, tactical, tactical. And at Chelsea, it was run, run, run and it was very difficult for me. With Chelsea, I always ran a bit more, and with Brighton we almost always had the ball, with Chelsea it was a different football, and we had to run more."

Pochettino's first game in charge of Man Utd, barring any unexpected changes, is expected to be against old rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22nd.

#1258. Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur

Did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

It was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be said of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

All of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

“Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi said. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We showed our maturity. We are improving.”

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

Spurs face Leeds United, Ipswich Town, Sunderland and Fulham in their next four league games. The momentum could, and perhaps should, continue to build. Their optimism here contrasted sharply with the angst of Palace, and with the troubled look that was etched on Sage’s face.

“Very pleased for the performance, very tough game. You don’t know 11 [against 11] would be different game but Crystal Palace are very tough because they defend with a low block, no space and we showed we are a mature team. When asked if Spurs are looking up the table, he replied: “We don’t forget the ambitions. We have to look behind what was the situation two weeks ago. In the last two years, two times 17th in the table, many games without a win in front of our fans. We have to stay focused. They are improving, increasing the level of performance.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Palace defender said: “Definitely was frustrating. It was one of the first tackles of the game. And we felt like we were doing well and it is unfortunate. We go again.

Gray is carded after slamming into Kamada with a late, sliding challenge. That was slighty reckless and Gray needs to be careful now.

Referee Oliver rules that the card has been upgraded from yellow to red. It was an ugly challenge as Mateta rashly caught Van de Ven on the achilles and collided with Van Hecke. Palace’s task looks very daunting now.

Jean-Philippe Mateta receives his first red card for Crystal Palace! 🟥 https://t.co/U9UYb29mbk

Van Hecke is very unhappy with the tackle and a scuffle nearly ensues after he also caught in the follow-through. The referee initially awards a yellow card, but he’s been sent over to the monitor. The Palace striker could be in trouble here.

Sharp and incisive football from Palace as Mateta tees up Kamada. The midfielder shoots from long range and his strike stings the palms of Kinsky, who gathers the ball with relative ease.

Palace’s defending has been their biggest problem this season but they have started well here, taking up a good shape and packing the areas in front of the penalty box.

It’s Tottenham with all the early possession, while Palace are sitting deep in a rigid five-back formation, plotting ways to hit their opponents on the counter-attack.

Tottenham win an early corner through Tel’s dribble. Henderson punches Mateus Fernandes’ delivery away to relieve the pressure on Palace.

We are under way in north London. Will Tottenham’s encouraging momentum continue or can Palace cause an upset?

Both squads are welcomed onto the pitch to huge applause. For the first time in a while, there’s a real sense of positivity around Spurs following the wins against Coventry and Chelsea.

Pierre Sage has only been in the job since June but his position is already in serious peril. There are some suggestions he could even lose his job tonight, if this game goes badly, although that remains to be seen. One wonders whether the likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank will be watching this game closely...

Could Spurs win three in a row in the Premier League? Three managers have come and gone since they last did so, 616 days ago. The home fans will be confident of achieving that feat against a Palace team that has the worst defensive record in the Premier League.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, had some good news for the supporters on Friday when he said that James Maddison was fit and available despite being taken off at Stamford Bridge. “This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.

“For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.”

While Tottenham are chasing a third successive league victory for the first time in 616 day, De Zerbi insisted there will be no complacency. “For me nothing has changed. We started this pre-season with a long project and we have to stay calm and clear in the head to work to build something better than when we came here,” he said. “One win or one defeat more, nothing will change. We have to analyse to improve the results but to improve the results we have to improve all aspects.”

Pierre Sage, the Palace manager, lightened the load after knocking Fulham out of the Carabao Cup in midweek but seemed surprised that the fans have remained so supportive. “It’s always a good sign,” he said. “I appreciate it [singing his name at Craven Cottage] very much and I can thank them but I prefer they are with the team than me alone. Because I’m the manager, but I’m not the most important part of the team, of the performance and the result. I think the players need it more than me but it’s really appreciated from me.”

Asked what he has learnt about fan sentiment from looking at social media, he said: “I think they understood what happened, why we are not perfect at the moment. We don’t care who is the most responsible for the situation. I take the responsibility. I have no problem with that. I just want people to understand what we do and why.”

Two changes from the starting line-up that took on Newcastle: captain Dean Henderson is back in goal and Oscar Mingueza replaces Anan Khalaili at right wing-back.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.

#1256. Some Man Utd Stars Wanted Unai Emery Instead of Mauricio Pochettino

A number of Manchester United players were hoping the club would appoint Unai Emery as their new head coach, according to a report.

United are expected to sack Michael Carrick following a dismal start to the season, according to GIVEMESPORT sources. Indeed, the Reds sit 18th in the Premier League table after winning just ONE of their opening 10 top-flight matches.

Carrick reported to training on Wednesday, but a decision has been made on his future with United expected to hold a meeting to inform the 45-year-old that he has been relieved of his duties.

With Carrick facing the axe, United are poised to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. It's believed the Reds are now finalising a move for the United States national team manager with an agreement in principle reached on personal terms.

Pochettino's USMNT contract contains a £7.5million release clause, though his backroom staff are expected to increase the overall cost of hire. The Argentine's current deal is set to expire in 2030, after the next World Cup.

With most of United's first-team players out on international duty with their respective countries, the squad anticipates that Pochettino will be their new head coach when they return.

However, according to talkSPORT, some United players were hoping for the appointment of Aston Villa boss Emery instead.

Emery, who was in the dugout for Villa's dramatic 4-4 draw against Carrick's United on Sunday, is in talks with the Villans over a new and improved contract, having done a superb job in the West Midlands.

The Spaniard took charge of Villa back in October 2022, following the dismissal of Steven Gerrard, and has since spearheaded the club back to the Champions League twice in three years and guided them to their first trophy in 25 years.

As for Carrick, he is yet to be given any clarity over his future. United CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox recommended a change of manager during a meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS in Monaco on Tuesday, but that decision hasn't been communicated to Carrick, who has been left in the dark.

Hansi Flick was certainly full of praise for Emery earlier this season, ahead of Barcelona hosting Villa in the Champions League.

It will also be difficult because they are managed by Unai Emery. He is one of the best coaches in Europe and the world.

"You look at his team, and they have a clear structure in both defence and attack. They have different patterns of play and are very dangerous."

United are on a run of just one win in 10 matches across all competitions, and that came in the 3-2 comeback success against Roma last Tuesday. Before that included damaging losses against Chelsea, Bournemouth and Como.

Should Pochettino be appointed, as expected, his first game in charge is set to be a daunting-looking trip to Anfield to face Liverpool after the November international break. That is followed by another away game, this time at Sporting CP in the Champions League.

#1255. The little-known new face called up by England: Can you name the star brought in to replace Ezri Konsa?

Published: 05:58 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 12:26 EST, 10 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel has made a first-time England call-up to replace Ezri Konsa - but casual fans could be forgiven if they do not recognise the latest Three Lions addition.

He is not a widely-recognised face among the stars from the Premier League and other top European leagues in Tuchel's selection but James Hill, 24, has starred for Bournemouth in their eight-match winning run under Marco Rose this season.

The central defender, who started his career at Fleetwood Town, has enjoyed a dream few months: He married partner Tara Rose in June, welcomed his first child in August and has now had his maiden England call.

England announced today that Arsenal defender Konsa will not be in contention to face Croatia at Wembley on Thursday night - although he will be fit to potentially face Spain away on Sunday - and Hill has been called up in his place.

Hill has played for England's Under 20s and Under 21s but this is his first senior call. He was signed by Bournemouth for just £1.2million in 2022 - beating Sheffield United, Burnley, Leeds, Southampton, Tottenham and even Barcelona, who all checked on his progress.

Bournemouth's official X account posted today: 'Congratulations, Hilly. Our defender has earned a first senior @England call-up.'

James Hill - pictured with new wife Tara - has been called up to the latest England squad (Source: Instagram/james_hill_10)

Hill has starred for Bournemouth in their eight-match winning run under Marco Rose

Hill's route to the top is a fascinating one. He attended a trial day at Fleetwood as a 14-year-old and managed to impress them enough to earn place at their new academy.

Interestingly, Hill did not play for a football team of any kind before he was 10, simply kicking a ball around with friends and playing in the garden to hone his skills.

Blackpool opted against signing him after a trial and he was then dropped by Bolton after a short stint.

It proved to be a shrewd piece of talent identification from Fleetwood, with Hill later becoming the club's record sale, eclipsing the fee they received for Jamie Vardy.

And having signed for the Cherries in 2022, Hill has now established himself as a key member of Marco Rose's side.

He's played every minute of every Premier League match this season at the heart of the defence and clearly Tuchel has been impressed.

Speaking before his call-up, Hill said: 'It’s every kid’s dream, isn’t it? You grow up watching the Three Lions on TV, for the World Cup, the Euros. It’s one of the greatest honours you can have in football.'

Football is in the blood for Hill. His father, Matt, made more than 550 appearances in the Football League for the likes of Preston North End, Wolverhampton Wanderers, Sheffield United and Queens Park Rangers as a defender.

Hill played for England at age group level, pictured here kissing his now wife after a game

Hill's younger brother, Tyler, is also in the game, playing for Torquay United in National League South.

But Matt did not pressure his sons into the sport, with James previously telling the Times: 'He didn’t want me to feel as though it’s a job.

'He wanted me to feel like I’m wanting to be here because I love doing it. This is my passion. It brings me happiness. He wanted me to come to that conclusion, not for him to make that decision for me.'

Hill was a well-rounded sportsman and his secondary school did not even play football. Instead, he excelled as a fly-half for the rugby side and impressed as a javelin thrower.

He attributes his success as being aided by trying his hand at different disciplines and it is paying off in abundance having had to largely bide his time before earning a first-team spot under Andoni Iraola last term, with loans to Blackburn and Hearts helping him develop.

Hill's progress flew somewhat under the radar somewhat for many fans outside of Bournemouth and his career peak of an England call-up coincides with domestic bliss.

Having married Tara in the summer, they welcomed their daughter Edie two months later.

Hill, pictured, heading the ball away against Ipswich has become one of the best defenders in the Premier League

'Becoming a dad is one of the most special things I’ve ever experienced in my life,' he said. 'There isn’t a manual though, it’s just like, "Congratulations, you’ve got a baby". Then the door shuts! Hang on a minute. What am I supposed to do next? Is there a book for this? My wife has been absolutely incredible.'

He regularly shares pictures from both his professional and personal life on social media, putting wedding snaps alongside action shots of Bournemouth games.

Hill's England call-up will no doubt introduce him to a whole new audience previously unaware of the defender's capabilities, with only 34,000 Instagram followers at present.

The 24-year-old must now impress Tuchel enough to earn some game time when England play Croatia on Thursday in their next Nations League encounter.

Gustav Isaksen is Lazio’s top priority for a new contract after the club extended Romano Floriani Mussolini’s deal until 2031.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, the leaders face a delicate situation, with around half the squad’s contracts due to expire within the next 18 months. Isaksen’s deal runs until 2028, and Lazio are ready to reward his best spell since joining the club. There’s less urgency with Nicolò Rovella. He has made only 12 appearances in 2026, totalling just over 600 minutes, and neither side is in a rush, although a decision will be needed by the end of the season. Fisayo Dele-Bashiru’s future also needs to be resolved.

Mattia Cataldi, Manuel Lazzari, Matteo Cancellieri and Luca Pellegrini all have contracts expiring in 2027 and could leave next summer. Josip Šutalo, Davide Frattesi and Albert Gudmundsson are on loan.

#1253. Man Utd ‘Up For Sale’ as Financial Expert Reveals the Glazers’ Asking Price

Manchester United fans remain disgruntled with the current ownership of the club, with another manager on the verge of the sack.

Michael Carrick is set to become the seventh permanent manager to be shown the exit door since Sir Alex Ferguson's reign ended in 2013.

However, many within the fan base are adamant that the real problem at Old Trafford is the hierarchy, and until that is in order, any manager will struggle to get the English giants back to the top of European football.

Protests took place inside the ground during United's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday. Green and gold balloons were deployed along with a banner, which read: "We don't want a new stadium, we want the owners out."

The Glazer family have been major shareholders in the club since Malcolm Glazer assumed full control in May 2005. They have been far from popular figures in Manchester, with debt mounting ever since they arrived.

Speaking to talkSPORT, financial expert Stefan Borson revealed that United fans hoping for the Glazers to sell could get their wish in the near future.

Michael Carrick is set to be sacked as Manchester United's head coach with Mauricio Pochettino in line to replace him at Old Trafford

Borson stated: "My understanding from somebody, a senior person in the game, told me that there is a process and that they are for sale.

"You would question why they wouldn't make it public, although when they last made a process public, that of course ended with a slightly disappointing outcome (Ratcliffe's shares)."

He went on to claim that the Glazers hadn't made their intentions public, which could be linked to the fallout from Sir Jim Ratcliffe's arrival in 2024. "They may be trying something different by not making it formal, but they are now accepting that now is the time," he said.

"They (Glazers) are robust, and they will only go when their price is met.

"They believe this is a club that has such a robust brand that even if they are unsuccessful on the pitch, it has very little difference to the commercial viability and ability to generate revenue."

Borson expects the asking price to be in the region of £5 billion, citing FSG's deal to sell 38% of Liverpool to the 1892 Holdings Consortium as a yardstick.

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of important saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

“I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

“We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

It was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

McGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations said it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

The Japanese international is Villa’s own version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson, who revolutionised English football with a vast range of passing from his own penalty area.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

Aston Villa manager, Unai Emery, is giving a full Premier League debut to Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka against Fulham this evening.

The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”

Emery had also made a cryptic remark about Nicolas Jackson and Johann Manzambi in his Friday press conference. The suggestion was that they had been merely rested for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth.

But the Spaniard said: “For different reasons, not only rest.”

Whatever he meant is unclear, but both start for Villa tonight.

Fulham have won their last two league games – against Hull and Coventry.

Villa are aiming to win three successive league games for the first time in this calendar year. The omens are good as they’ve beaten Fulham in their last seven league meetings at Villa Park.

Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

#1251. Pochettino Can Lead New Era at Man Utd With Move for Cole Palmer to Replace Bruno Fernandes

Manchester United are set to enter a new era at Old Trafford, as they close in on the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils are expected to sack manager Michael Carrick this week after he led the team to just one win in 10 Premier League games so far this season, leaving the team 18th in the table heading into the international break.

GIVEMESPORT sources understand that United chiefs have reached an agreement on personal terms with Pochettino, with the contract he signed with the USMNT in the summer to continue as their manager until 2030 containing a $10m (£7.4m) release clause. The Argentine is keen to take over at Old Trafford.

Should he sign on the dotted line to be the man in the dugout, Pochettino will have some major issues to sort out. A number of defensive signings are needed in 2027, with INEOS reportedly planning a rebuild in the summer.

That leads on from Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw all being out of contract at the end of the current season, while there are doubts about the long-term futures of Noussair Mazraoui, Matthijs De Ligt, and Diogo Dalot, who was booed off by fans in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend.

There is also a need to bolster the attack. Joshua Zirkzee's future looks bleak, Marcus Rashford will be entering the final year of his contract, Amad hasn't scored a goal in almost a full calendar year, and Bruno Fernandes' contract is set to expire, with talks over an extension having stalled.

A Bruno exit is not something the club will be hoping for, but it is certainly more possible now than it was a few months ago. There is said to be interest from a number of clubs in Europe and in Saudi Arabia, while the player himself could be tempted considering his age.

Should he move on, then replacing his goals and assists would immediately need to become a priority for the recruitment department. Players like Nico Paz and Morgan Gibbs-White have been linked with stepping up to the plate, but the strongest link has come in the shape of Chelsea sensation Cole Palmer.

The former Man City academy star grew up as a Man Utd fan and was understood to be open to making the move to Old Trafford last summer, before Fernandes committed his future to United, and he then signed a new extension at Stamford Bridge.

But it was Pochettino who took Palmer to Stamford Bridge and coached him to become one of the franchise players in the division, and a reunion could be something beneficial to both players.

Since moving to Chelsea, Palmer has thrived as the main man at the heart of everything. Much like Bruno, he is the focal point of every attack. But he has some attributes that Fernandes doesn't have, which make him a better fit in the modern game.

Palmer is a far better dribbler and is capable of beating players one-on-one, while he is also capable of getting goals and assists when playing in a wider position. That would allow for more tactical flexibility depending on match situations or availability.

He's also just 24 years old, meaning he still has the best part of a decade to go in his career, when he could be playing at the very highest level. Fernandes, meanwhile, is on the way down, as his performances this season have shown.

Any deal would obviously be incredibly difficult to do. Chelsea won't want to sell their best player, and especially not to a direct rival. But with the player's buy-in, it's possible. INEOS could make a major statement by bringing him in, filling an instant hole in the squad, and upgrading.

Pochettino would be getting a player he knows well and can get the best out of, and together they can lead a new era at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino is a leading contender to take over as Man Utd manager, and he already has his own Dele Alli at Old Trafford.

#1250. Former Napoli striker Sosa: ‘Højlund can’t improve if he trains with Lucca’

Former Napoli striker Roberto Sosa believes Rasmus Højlund can’t improve while his only competition is Lorenzo Lucca, and he wants the club to sign Monza’s Gustavo Varela in January.

According to Areanapoli, the Argentine, nicknamed ‘Pampa’, made the comments on Radio Marte. Lucca has been heavily criticised, and Troy Deeney called him “one of the worst strikers I’ve ever seen” earlier this week.

“Would Monza’s Gustavo Varela be the right signing in January? It’s easy to say yes,” Sosa said. “Højlund can’t play every game. If you want the Dane to improve, you have to put him up against someone strong in training during the week.

“How is he going to improve competing with Lucca? Maybe Lorenzo can improve that way, but not him. Lucca to Lecce? He’d struggle to be a starter there too.”

Napoli have already contacted the representatives of Varela, who leads Serie A with nine goals and has just earned his first Portugal call-up. Lucca, meanwhile, is expected to leave on loan.

“Varela could be a useful signing to increase the competition up front and raise Rasmus’ level,” Sosa added. “I like Højlund, but are you really convinced he can score eight to 10 goals in the next few games?”

Højlund missed a great chance from two yards in Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Lazio.

#1249. Michael Owen Named the Two England Teammates he Still ‘Resents’

Michael Owen admitted he still feels 'resentment' towards two former England colleagues, despite having been retired from the game for over a decade.

The ex-Liverpool and Real Madrid striker was left disappointed by his teammates' actions during the Three Lions' 1998 World Cup campaign.

England were knocked out of the tournament in the Round of 16 after a penalty shootout loss against Argentina. The game became infamous for David Beckham's controversial red card for kicking out at Argentine midfielder Diego Simeone.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Michael Owen scored 40 goals in 89 appearances for England's senior team.

Over two decades after the incident, Becks is one of the players Owen still holds ill feelings towards. Speaking to Simon Jordan on his Up Front podcast, the 46-year-old revealed:

"Firstly, I don't believe David Beckham's kick out at Diego Simeone should've been a red card, but that is irrelevant. He made a mistake and that is where my resentment lies.

"For a lot of players you only get one shot at a World Cup, and he made a big mistake – he would admit that. You could say that it contributed to us being knocked out and that is a big thing."

Focusing on the same game, Owen also pointed out another ex-teammate he holds a grudge against to this day. Paul Ince was one of the unfortunate two England players to miss a spot-kick during the penalty shootout against Argentina.

Owen stated: "You can resent a lot of things if you use that word, and I do resent a lot of things. Paul Ince missed a penalty and I resent him choosing to shoot the ball one way instead of the other, in the same way, I resent Beckham making the decision to kick out at Simeone."

Michael Owen played with some of the greatest players of his generation, but three stand out above the rest

The man who exploded onto the international scene in the 1998 World Cup, Owen, is adamant his nation would've progressed to the quarter-finals had Beckham not had his moment of madness:

"I resent his actions for all manner of reasons. It was a mistake that only he made, and it makes you think that if he hadn't done it, we could have beaten Argentina. I'm absolutely convinced that we would've beaten them with 11 men because we were the better team."

Michael Owen England Stats with David Beckham and Paul Ince

Interestingly enough, Owen also played with Beckham at Real Madrid, but they shared the pitch just 27 times, combining for only two goals. They spent a bit more time together on the field of play for the Three Lions, and at least combined for six goals.

That's better than his relationship with Ince, the pair failed to ever set up one another – perhaps highlighting their lack of relationship.

#1248. Como sporting director Ludi: ‘Business with Real Madrid adds value to our football’

Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi says the club’s close ties with Real Madrid are good for Italian football as a whole, and he has confirmed that Jacobo Ramón will stay at the club for the rest of the season.

According to the Corriere dello Sport, the Lariani’s relationship with Real Madrid has been one of the keys to their rise. They have brought in Nico Paz and Ramón from the Spanish giants, and Roma are now trying to sign Endrick from them.

“We have a great relationship with them,” Ludi said. “The basis isn’t so much the relationship with Real itself, but the valuable relationships we’ve built, both with prestigious clubs and within our own club. We take care of relationships. It isn’t something you can take for granted.

“The Nico Paz deal was a win-win situation. We had the chance to invest in a player with great potential, and they believed in our technical project, thanks partly to Fàbregas’ credibility and ability.

“I’ve never commented on other clubs’ deals, but it’s significant that talent can be brought to Italy. Como are an example of how young players can help you achieve very important results. This year, young players have a much higher share of minutes than in recent seasons, and that’s a very good sign for Serie A.”

Ramón received his first Spain call-up this week, but Ludi says the defender isn’t going anywhere for now.

“When we went to negotiate for Nico Paz, there was an update on his position, and he’ll definitely stay with us for the whole season. It’s still too early to know what his future might hold.”

Como aren’t planning any major signings in January. Instead, they’re waiting for Moise Kean, Assane Diao and Jesús Rodríguez to return from injury.

“We may look at outgoing deals for players who aren’t getting much game time. In terms of signings, we don’t have anything incredible planned. We’re very happy with the squad. If an opportunity came up and we needed small improvements, we could act, but I’d mainly back the players we already have.”

Ludi also highlighted Como’s commitment to Italian youngsters. Riccardo Cassano has earned an Italy call-up, and Papaccioli scored in the Champions League.

Sunday’s defeat at San Siro left Fàbregas’ side six points behind Inter, but Ludi was full of praise for the champions.

“We’ve had an extraordinary start to the season. Our challenge was to stay competitive while playing every three days, and our Champions League run shows we’ve managed that. Inter are the strongest team in Italy, and they approached the game extraordinarily well. We need to improve and grow. I’m sure we’ll learn from that game too.”

#1247. Jude Bellingham says he 'wants to be a gentleman' but admits he doesn't feel 'mature' because 'I can't cook, I can't drive and I rely on my family' in new smouldering photoshoot

Published: 10:54 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 13:36 EST, 10 November 2026

Real Madrid and England star Jude Bellingham has admitted he doesn't feel 'mature', despite being labelled as such from a young age.

The midfielder, 23, has impressed with his level head and assured public speaking since breaking onto the professional scene at 16 and living under the glare of the public eye in his formative years.

But Bellingham has confessed that his complete attention to detail as a footballer has left deficiencies in other areas of his life, such as cooking or driving.

Speaking to Vogue in an interview accompanying a fashion photoshoot in which he's dressed to fit the 60s and 70s aesthetic he leans into, Bellingham also spoke about his desire to be a role model for the younger generation.

'I feel mature in a football context because I’ve played nearly 400 games, but in a life context I don’t feel that mature now, to be honest,' he told Vogue.

'I can’t cook, I can’t drive… I’m good at what I do, but everything else? Not that great. I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff – chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else.

Jude Bellingham poses for Vogue during a photoshoot displaying his love of 60s fashion

Bellingham admits he isn't mature in some areas of his life - seen here holding up his provisional driving licence

'That’s where I’m at. I work hard every day and all day, and then when I get home, I’ve probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things. But there’ll be a time and a place for that, I’m sure.'

Bellingham plays with a fierce competitive spirit on the pitch but is aware of his responsibility to behave away from football, adding: 'I’ve always said that, off the pitch, I want to be a gentleman.'

The Real superstar, who is in a relationship with American influencer and model Ashlyn Castro, went on: 'You can’t just behave how you want but then still represent a city or a country every time you wear their shirt, because you are inspiring [someone].

'Whether you like it or not, you are looked up to by the next generation. I prefer to see it as a privilege.'

The photoshoot for the fashion magazine showcased Bellingham's sense of style, which he says is rooted in his admiration for iconic characters from the 60s and 70s such as Elvis Presley, Michael Caine and James Bond movies of the era.

The Vogue cover shows Bellingham in a dark brown suit and coat with wide lapels and a bright orange cardigan, while he appears in a herringbone overcoat and white chino shorts in another.

Another image shows Bellingham holding up his green provisional driving licence.

Bellingham, selected in the England squad for upcoming internationals against Croatia and Spain, is in a rich vein of form.

Bellingham is pictured in a sharp suit and says he is inspired by iconic figures of yesteryear

The cover star feels a responsibility to be a gentleman and positive role model

Under Jose Mourinho's management at the Bernabeu this season, he's scored four goals and provided four assists already in LaLiga, with the Spanish giants three points behind Barcelona in the title race.

He's joined in the England squad by his younger brother, Jobe, and is flying high for the national side now his relationship with Tuchel is on an even keel.

Last Friday, the Three Lions manager said: 'It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place.

'I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable he would not perform on that level.

'In the moment you see he's happy to come into camp, he's happy with the role he has, he's fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them is just the next step. I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach!'

On Jobe being called up from the Under-21s, he added: 'Yeah Jude and I have spoken about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream to play with Jobe for England.

'Jude was always saying: "Watch him, watch him he's good, he can make it". 'I would say: "Yeah we are watching him".

Bellingham poses in more casual attire, pairing a vintage Adidas sweater with pin stripe trousers

#1245. De Laurentiis contacts Cairo over Cacciamani as Napoli also chase Varela

Napoli have contacted Torino about winger Alessio Cacciamani, and Monza’s Gustavo Varela is their dream target as they plan for January.

According to Corriere dello Sport, Aurelio De Laurentiis has spoken directly to his Torino counterpart Urbano Cairo about the 19-year-old. Cacciamani is a product of Torino’s academy, a right-footed winger who plays on the left, and he has started 11 of the club’s 12 games in Serie A and the Coppa Italia, with a goal and an assist. He’s also an Italy Under-21 international.

Cacciamani won’t come cheap. Torino rejected a bid of around €12m from Roma in the summer and asked for at least €20m, and his value has only risen since.

Varela leads Serie A with nine goals and has 11 in all competitions. He’s valued at €25-30m, and former club Benfica hold a sell-on clause plus the right to match any offer.

However, Monza CEO Mauro Baldissoni wants to keep him: “The aim is to keep him with us until the end of the season. There are no negotiations, it’s all very premature, but the market is dynamic.”

Napoli’s interest in a left winger could also be linked to Noa Lang’s uncertain future following his clash with supporters during Sunday’s draw with Lazio. Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens remains on the list too.

#1244. Arsenal nous frustrates Liverpool as 14-year Anfield hoodoo ends with statement win

It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

“The mission was something we didn’t complete in 14 years,” Mikel Arteta said, having famously – in an Amazon documentary series – played You’ll Never Walk Alone to his players as they walked out to train to try and overcome a perceived mental block.

“There are reasons for that. Some of it psychological, some of it moments we did not nail on the pitch,” the Arsenal manager added of the winless run.

The result means that the north Londoners have already now won away at Villa Park, the Stadium of Light, the City Ground and Anfield. Stadiums where they dropped points last season. And that feels ominous.

A win would maybe have thrust Liverpool into the title race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, and with an evolving young team – with promising 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni handed his league debut – they are already nine points behind after just nine matches.

It is also clear, however, that they could have prevented this defeat having somehow been denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was blatantly pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross.

Referee Andy Madley may have missed it, but what was the excuse of Stuart Attwell, the VAR? It was a stunningly poor decision – another bad day for Pro Ref and the use of technology.

It might be argued that Timber did not pull hard enough to prevent Isak from reaching the ball. But the defender grabbed the shirt and continued to hold it for a long time. It had to be a penalty. Little wonder Iraola said Isak should dive next time. Who can blame him?

What is also clear and obvious is that, once again, Arsenal’s resilience, defensive determination and appetite for toughing it out will be their greatest weapons. They are certainly, under Arteta, not here to win friends – just to win matches and trophies.

“That defensive line, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It’s something I have never seen before,” Declan Rice, who was also a stand-out performer and delivered a fine assist for the winner, said.

Arsenal’s version of the Yellow Wall was, indeed, hugely impressive – it is now six clean sheets from their nine league games and, despite all their pressure, Liverpool did not have a shot on target. That has never happened in the Premier League since such statistics started to be compiled in 2003 (422 games ago).

“That’s incredible. It did not feel like it on the pitch. Again, it’s the commitment of every single player,” Arteta said. And that was indisputable.

Even the expected second-half momentum, the expected surge of attack after attack as Liverpool faced the Kop, crashed on Arsenal’s back line. The visitors were so well-drilled that they stifled space – they refused to crumble.

Arsenal put their bodies on the line with blocks and tackles and a bit of time-wasting. There were dark arts, especially from both centre-halves with Gabriel going unpunished after claiming he was struck in the face by Isak early on – VAR anyone? – and the otherwise outstanding Ezri Konsa throwing himself to the ground after minimal contact from the Liverpool centre-forward.

In fairness there was also a bit of that from an increasingly frustrated Liverpool with Alexis Mac Allister going down after touching heads with Noni Madueke, having already tried to provoke Martin Odegaard with a hand to the head when the Arsenal captain was on the turf. That was not good from Mac Allister either.

And the only goal? Again, more frustration for Liverpool. It was well-constructed from Arsenal, but only after Alisson Becker’s loose goal kick, aimed towards Jérémy Jacquet, who was slow to react, was intercepted by Odegaard with Bruno Guimarães poking the ball to the right, where it was collected by Madueke.

There was an overlap by Rice and his low centre was precise and dangerous across the face of the six-yard area, with Virgil van Dijk unsure what to do. It ran beyond the far post where Kai Havertz side-footed home.

"Absolutely brilliant from Arsenal." Kai Havertz gives Arsenal an early lead at Anfield! ⚡️ https://t.co/eeyhRcLlel

That was the hosts’ last tangible opportunity to score. As well as Arsenal defended, it was not a good afternoon for Liverpool’s forwards, Bradley Barcola in particular, although it was interesting to see Arsenal double-up on Rio Ngumoha when he came on. Here is a question I did not think I would be asking at any stage this season: will Liverpool win the Premier League?

It would be premature to describe this Sunday’s Anfield fixture as a title duel. Arsenal are better equipped to defend their crown, while Liverpool are a work in progress.

Whatever the outcome this weekend, Arsenal will leave Merseyside as the overwhelming favourites to claim back-to-back titles. They have a six-point lead over Liverpool. Should that extend to nine, Andoni Iraola’s primary objective coming into this season will remain unchanged; qualifying for the Champions League will represent a promising start to his reign.

What makes this weekend more significant is the champions will find a different Anfield to that which ended last season in such a downbeat mood, and came into this one uncertain of what was in store.

The discussion about what is achievable for Liverpool in the coming months is evolving by the week, the team bubbling along slightly under the radar.

There are several reasons why there are those who believe Iraola’s side might push Arsenal closer than anticipated.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool, who start the game in fifth with 15 points, and Arsenal, six points in front of them in second place. Anfield, that glorious night in May 1989 excepted, has not been the happiest of hunting grounds for Arsenal and though their record there recently – three draws in the last four visits – has perked up, they have gone 13 seasons without a victory, so long ago, in fact, that Mikel Arteta was in the side that celebrated Lukas Podolski  and Santo Cazorla earning them a 2-0 win.

Having already lost within the perimeter of the historic county of Lancashire this week, when knocked out of the Carabao Cup on penalties by League Two Fleetwood Town, the champions will be keen to end that barren streak and go into the 4.30pm kick-off on the back of three successive league victories following their defeat by Brighton. Points today, one or three, will put them ahead of Manchester City at the top of the table while victory for Liverpool would allow them to overtake Chelsea and move one point behind Brighton, the team they beat last week with the kind of performance that inspired talk of a credible title campaign.

For the visitors Max Dowman is suspended after his red card at Highbury and Bukayo Saka and William Saliba are sidelined for at least another three weeks with injury. In his pre-match press conference Arteta noted concerns about Noni Madueke (ankle), Declan Rice (thigh). Riccardo Calafiori (unspecified) and Christos Tzolis who has returned to training but all are expected to be available. Andoni Iraola has ruled out Jeremie Frimpong as well as long-term casualties Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley but hopes to be able to include Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Muñoz.
