#1195. Spain face England decider without Rodri, Olmo and Eric García as three uncapped players called up

Spain go into the Nations League decider for top spot against England without the injured Barcelona trio of Rodri, Dani Olmo and Eric García. Luis de la Fuente has handed first senior call-ups to two Betis players and to Real Madrid academy product Jacobo Ramón.

Víctor Muñoz is the fourth player ruled out through injury. Spain arrive in form. They came from behind to win 2-1 in Croatia on 6 October, with Mikel Merino scoring both goals. That made it 11 wins in a row. England beat Czechia 3-0 on the same night, with Harry Kane scoring twice.

Valles, 29, will compete for a place in goal. He has played every minute for Betis this season: 11 league games and all four of their games in the top European competition. Roca turns 30 on 26 November, and his call-up follows a long run of injuries. Jacobo Ramón, the third newcomer, plays in defence for Como and came through the Real Madrid academy.

Valles is one of four goalkeepers in the group. Barcelona’s Joan García is also back between the posts after injury kept him out of the previous squad. Pedro Porro, Nico Williams and Ferran Torres return for the same reason.

Pablo Barrios of Atlético and Ander Barrenetxea of Real Sociedad are also recalled.

Some familiar names are missing for other reasons. Marcos Llorente is absent because he has retired from international football.

The absences in midfield are the most striking. Without Rodri and Olmo, the call for Roca gives De la Fuente another option in the centre of the pitch. Pedri and Fermín are both included.

Several of the squad will be in action on Sunday before joining up. Atlético host Barcelona at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano on Sunday 8 November at 21:00. It is LaLiga matchday 12.

The game carries real weight at the top of the table. Barcelona lead the league on 30 points. Atlético have won their last seven league matches and can go top with an eighth.

#1192. Güler scores and assists as Real Madrid win at Mestalla to draw level with Barcelona

Arda Güler scored once and set up another as José Mourinho's Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 to reach 30 points, level with Barcelona, before the international break. Valencia are second from bottom in their last season at Mestalla.

Federico Valverde put Madrid ahead at Mestalla in the 28th minute on Saturday 7 November 2026. Güler doubled the lead eight minutes later. Jude Bellingham reached the byline and pulled the ball back. Güler met it first time and finished with his right foot.

Güler could have had more. Stole Dimitrievski stopped him twice: a strong shot from the edge of the area in the 43rd minute and a one-on-one in the 54th.

Kylian Mbappé’s strike in the 75th minute made it three. That goal stretched his scoring run to seven matches in a row. He has 12 league goals, three behind Barcelona’s Raphinha at the top of the scoring chart.

The visitors had 68% of the ball and completed 568 passes to Valencia’s 225. They took 19 shots, 11 of them on target. Valencia managed four shots and just two on target. Expected goals finished 2.39 to 0.26 in Madrid’s favour.

The hosts’ best moment came around the 20th minute. Aaron Mayol won the ball just outside the area and forced Thibaut Courtois to stretch for a save. Aguirre sent on Luis Rioja for Justin de Haas at half-time, but the pattern did not change.

The game grew bad-tempered. Valencia committed 26 fouls to Madrid’s six, and Aguirre himself was booked for dissent in the 59th minute. In the club’s own view, the punishment for Gayà’s challenge on Mbappé was harsh. Seven yellow cards were shown in all, four of them in a two-minute spell after the red card.

Two wins from 12 league games is all Valencia have to show so far. Only Malaga, on 5 points, are below them. Aguirre has one win from his five league games in charge. The club is already promoting season-ticket prices for the new Nou Mestalla.

The coach is concerned about the home form. Aguirre told EFE he was worried about failing to win any of his three matches at Mestalla. He added that Valencia were short of points with six games left in the first half of the season.

Three goals 🟰 Three points @emirates pic.twitter.com/KepMmEJqB4

— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 7, 2026

Madrid’s run has kept them in a three-way race at the top. Barcelona have played 11 games to Madrid’s 12 and sit top on goal difference. Atlético Madrid are third, two points behind with a game in hand.

#1185. IAN HERBERT: Classless Chuckle Brothers Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada are not fit to lace Michael Carrick's boots - they have treated a dignified Man United legend shamefully with this painful charade

Published: 07:34 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:39 EST, 11 November 2026

Both Michael Carrick and the man who has decided to sack him were present on Saturday night at a 40th anniversary dinner for Sir Alex Ferguson, staged in the dining suite where the Old Trafford dressing rooms used to be. It was lost on no one that Carrick, oozing class and humour that evening, spoke far better than Omar Berrada, Manchester United’s chief executive.

There were 100 or so present and Carrick had just been through the wringer of the 3-2 win over Roma but he did not let his predicament obscure the bigger picture. Carrick ‘spoke brilliantly’, actor James Nesbitt, who was also present, related. ‘The Roma result had just happened, but he showed a real gratitude to Sir Alex. He spoke with confidence and humour, but also with a real understanding of the enormity of what he achieved.’

Those who really understand United would not have been surprised. In the days when it was a classy, brilliantly run club, Carrick was the one who, perhaps more than any other senior player, would always look out for the rank-and-file staff – ensuring that the backroom teams were taken out for a drink at the end of the season, and that taxis home were laid on.

It was he who latched on to what was good about the Manchester United ‘family,’ ensuring that everyone from the reception staff to the laundry team were made to feel a part of it. Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos have clinically dismantled the old sense of a United ‘community' but Carrick’s return created a gratifying sense around Old Trafford, back in January, that it was perhaps not entirely dead.

All of which contributes to the unalloyed rage that many who love the club will be feeling today about the shameful and classless treatment of Carrick. A man forced through the ritual of driving into the training ground at 7.15am this morning by Berrada and United director of football Jason Wilcox – men not fit to lace his boots – when the whole world knows he is toast.

As Carrick, a professional to his core, went through this painful charade, Berrada and Wilcox – the Statler and Waldorf of the modern Manchester United – had had their secretaries arrange air travel to Monaco today for a meeting with Ratcliffe, which could not be brought forward.

Michael Carrick oozes class and humility but has been dragged through a painful charade by his superiors

Omar Berrada (left) and Jason Wilcox (right) are the the Statler and Waldorf of the modern Manchester United

There have been moments amid the recent tempest which point to United requiring a more commanding manager for the depths that Ratcliffe and his dismal men have reduced the club to. I could see from my vantage point close to the United dugout at their trip to Chelsea, two weeks back, that Carrick simply didn’t have the words to steer the ship away from that afternoon’s disaster.

But in the faces of men like Kobbie Mainoo and, before injury, Marcus Rashford, who have been restored to life and self-belief as United players, we have also witnessed Carrick’s faculty to see and know quality in players and give it full force.

A year ago, we were witnessing Ruben Amorim, the manager hired at vast expense by Ratcliffe’s football geniuses, run down Mainoo’s United career. In the insane mayhem of Sunday afternoon's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, he was the team’s creative anchor.

The people who have actually mattered at United – the fanbase – appreciate the respect Carrick warrants. It’s why the anthem carrying his name was still coming down from the Stretford End and the old North Stand on Sunday.

And so, of course, does Sir Alex, even though you half suspect he wondered all along if Carrick had quite the bite for the toughest job in world football, while hoping against hope he’d thrive.

‘There is a casualness about him that causes people to misunderstand his value and his constitution,’ Ferguson wrote of Carrick in his autobiography. ‘His handicap was, I feel, that he lacked the bravado of Frank Lampard and Steven Gerrard. But his character has always been outstanding. He's a football man.’ Sir Alex considered Carrick a better player than both those two.

And now what you suspect will be Carrick’s valedictory days at the club he has served so well are presided over by executives whose own fitness for purpose at Old Trafford was an open question from the start.

Very few people around Manchester City viewed the loss of Berrada, their ‘chief football officer’, as something to be fearful about, when Ratcliffe decided to make him United’s chief executive in 2024. Some former City insiders privately wondered how on earth he’d landed a job of that kind.

‘There is a casualness about him that causes people to misunderstand his value and his constitution,’ Sir Alex Ferguson wrote of Carrick in his autobiography

Sir Alex considered Carrick a better player than both Frank Lampard and Steven Gerrard

United want to tell Carrick ‘face to face’ what the whole world knows. These people won’t even discern what gross disrespect they are affording a man who deserves far better

And if Ratcliffe thought he was accessing City’s intellectual property when recruiting Jason Wilcox as technical director, then that was dodgy logic, too. Wilcox had only run City’s academy – a grossly incomparable challenge. His comparable experience to the United role was a mere 15 months as Southampton’s director of football. They were in the Championship for some of that time.

These were the men jetting out to Ratcliffe’s tax haven to tell him who should and should not manage United. Thus subjecting Carrick to another phantom training session at the Carrington – two weeks after watching the Under 21s play there while those Chuckle Brothers put their heads together about sacking him, across the complex.

United are putting it around, would you believe, that they want to be seen to be ‘doing the right thing’ and ‘observing the right process’. Well frankly, many inside football view this leadership group’s decision making as an embarrassment.

Nesbitt expressed sympathy for Carrick. ‘I feel for him,’ he said. ‘I'm no pundit but I am a fan. Clearly there's dissatisfaction with the fans about what we perceive is going on, but I think he's trying his best.’

United want to tell Carrick ‘face to face’ what the whole world knows. These people won’t even discern what gross disrespect they are affording a man who deserves far better.

Declan Rice has now been booked for a hand in the face of Sadilek, or possibly for kicking the ball away after the referee blew his whistle. Slavia Prague continue to ask questions, but David Raya has not been stretched.

Mosquera with a strong recovery run to defend against Ayaosi in the corner at the expense of a throw-in. It feels like Arsenal are through their rough patch at the start of the half, but Arteta will want the third.

Here come some Arsenal changes: Mosquera on for Konsa (who has been booked), and Tzolis on for Eze.

Slavia’s man-to-man pressing has been far more suffocating in this half, but there was a reminder there that when Arsenal get it right there is space to attack. Raya almost sold Rice short, but he whipped a ball around the corner first time to Merino, who played forward. Still no Arsenal changes.

Slavia Prague enjoying a period of possession but it is all in front of Arsenal.

Then Madueke loses the ball in a promising position, and Ayaosi is running right at the Arsenal back four. Konsa partially blocks his shot, but it deflects behind for a corner. Good delivery over Raya, but it bounces out for a goal kick.

Konsa with a storming run forward and a floated cross as Arsenal come alive as an attacking force, but it breaks down with a Ben White foul on the edge of the box.

Ezri Konsa booked after Ayaosi gets to a loose ball first near the touchline. Moments before that, White and Raya messed about with the ball and there were some choice words from Rice and Arteta. Arsenal have dropped their standards so far in the half.

Arteta is really raging on the touchline. He is not happy with how Arsenal have started this second half. He just aimed a few verbals at White for a defensive mix-up. White had actually already received an apology from Raya and didn’t seem to think it was his fault.

Rice with a chance to pick out Madueke on the counter but his diagonal pass was cut out. Slavia have been sent out with a flea in their ear, and have been much improved so far. Arteta will want Arsenal to stay serious and weather this spell.

Tonight has been a reminder of how good Martin Zubimendi is in the air. He’s wearing a face mask because of a broken nose but he’s won every header he has gone for. He’s not particularly tall but he has a great leap and timing.

Slavia Prague have a free-kick on the edge of Arsenal’s box after Konsa goes sliding in. Much more like it from Slavia Prague early on, Arsenal a little dozy since the restart.

Kubiak shoots low from the free-kick, but it is straight into the wall.

The home crowd have something to shout about for the first time tonight. Kubiak brings a decent save out of David Raya after shooting with his left foot from 25 yards. Then Raya slices a kick out for a throw-in.

Slavia have made a double sub: Suleiman and Sturm off, N’Guessan and Chytil on.

From the early stages of the game, the home team have tried to sprint up to the ball and pressure Arsenal, but they have been manipulated and played through so easily at times. When they do lock on man-to-man, Arsenal are hitting Madueke, Eze and Gyokeres early who are pinning defenders and then laying the ball off to runners.

Arsenal are dispatching another Champions League league phase opponent with ease, but the big positive has been the performances of Eze, Gyokeres and Madueke. Without Saka, Arteta needs them to step up and provide goals and assists. Albeit against poor opposition, they have all looked dangerous. Might we see half-time changes with Saturday’s game against Hull in mind?

Kubiak down and there are loud appeals for a Slavia free-kick but the referee was not having any of it. Gyokeres proves an otlet again, but his pass towards Madueke was too strong.

Arsenal have a corner and they are rampant. Eze with a flick around the corner which almost finds Gyokeres, they are playing with plenty of attacking panache. The quality of opposition needs accounting for but Arteta will be delighted given he made six changes.

Gabriel then threatens after Domchak spills Madueke’s cross, but his effort was blocked.

Arsenal wasted a counter initially with Eze running into a Zubimendi pass but they kept it alive and eventually punished their hosts. Merino with a cute pass back into Gyokeres’s path, and he took his time before curling a shot in off the far post. Arsenal should not be caught from here.

If you thought the Gyokeres assist was good, then that goal was even better. Gorgeous finish. That takes him to three assists and two goals in his past five games.

What a finish from Viktor Gyökeres from a tight angle 📐🎯 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/EET5P7aJ2X

Slavia Prague have had their first shot: Holes poking wide after a long throw was hurled into the box. Not much more than a half chance.

The referee is now having a word with Rice after he complained about Eze not being awarded a free-kick. Slavia have settled down a touch after that very rocky period, but they are still to muster a shot on goal.

Declan Rice is throwing a blanket over any flickering embers of a Slavia Prague attack, and then he is running the game from there. Arsenal’s captain on the night has been imperious so far.

Now Declan Rice feeds the ball straight through the six-yard box but Hincapie could not quite make it his to score a tap-in. Surely a question of when not if Arsenal put this game to bed.

Eze and Madueke are feeling it tonight. Slavia’s full-backs have been going through footballing hell in this opening half an hour.

Eze and Hincapie’s turn to cause problems down the left, the left-back’s pull-back evaded everyone, before Eze sat down the defender in the box but his shot was blocked.

Then Domchak saves from point-blank range to deny Merino! Slick play between Madueke and White to carve out the chance.

Arsenal really should have buried the second.

Domchak claimed Rice’s cross from the free-kick and Slavia Prague tried to counter-attack, but it was really diligent defensive work from Madueke to snuff out the danger. Arsenal continue to look in complete control.

Madueke then proves a thorn in the Slavia defence’s side, sitting down the left-back and standing up a cross to the back post. Gyokeres won the header, then Merino glanced over.

A moment of promise from Slavia Prague, but their pull-back to the edge of the box is picked up by Arsenal and Eze skips through a couple of challenges before being brought down by Moses. Yellow card for the Slavia Prague midfielder.

Then Ayaosi concedes a cheap free-kick against Hincapie, in a crossing position wide left.

Arsenal leaving themselves light at the back, but White, Gabriel and Konsa are happy dealing with the one-on-one duels, they look physically stronger than the Slavia forwards. Madueke, aside from his goal, has been very tidy on the ball so far.

Sharp interplay from Gyokeres and Eze again, teeing up Merino to sting the palms of the goalkeeper with a shot from the edge of the box. Arsenal corner.

Last time out in the Champions League against Lille, Arsenal’s squad players in attack failed to seize their chance but this has been much more promising from them.

Domchak makes a scrambling save on the line to stop Arsenal going two up, and possibly killing the game. Zubimendi’s break forward created the danger, and Gyokeres and Hincapie were close to applying the finish.

There was a moment just after scoring where Hincapie was caught forward on the overlap, and who else but Declan Rice was on hand to mop up the counter-attack in the left-back zone? Order restored, and Arsenal back on top in the game soon after.

Slavia Prague make a mess of a simple long ball forward, disobeying the old maxim that says never let the ball bounce. Gyokeres was alive though, hooking the ball behind the defence with a clever early pass. Madueke’s pace was always going to send him clear, and he slipped the ball through the legs of the goalkeeper Domchak.

That didn’t take long. Arsenal have dominated the ball in these opening exchanges and now they have scored with their first real chance. It’s a lovely pass by Gyokeres, who is not known for his intricate build-up play, and Madueke’s pace gets him behind. Madueke’s third goal of the season.

With Merino, Zubimendi and Rice in Arsenal’s midfield, there is perhaps no natural creator, but the three of them are rotating, taking it in turns to stand between the centre-backs or go high.

Madueke stands up a cross which Slavia Prague head clear. Most of the game is being played in the home team’s half, which you would expect. Arsenal probing and moving the ball patiently.

Madueke and Ben White then combine well, but Eze cannot quite let fly from a central position. The Arsenal left-winger drifting across the line to receive the ball in that move.

Quite an industrious start from the home team, trying to close Arsenal down, but Merino and Zubimendi combined well in a tight space to help Arsenal move forward. The flag goes up against Ben White for offside, possibly mistakenly.

At the other end Sturm caused Konsa a problem, but the Arsenal defender recovered well and the goal kick decision was in his favour too, much to the annoyance of the home crowd.

Arsenal also paid their respects at Colney to the 30-year-old Spanish player who died after a collision with the Andorra’s goalkeeper.

Declan Rice is wearing the captain’s armband and leads Arsenal out at a smoky Fortuna Arena. Slavia Prague are celebrating their 144th birthday, and marked the occasion with a choir and classical music.

William Saliba is BACK 💥 https://t.co/aRmJoIlxSc

Liverpool twice threw away a lead to lose against Fenerbahce in Istanbul. That has some relevance to Arsenal because Liverpool are one of the teams above them in the league phase table. Win in Prague, and they will move one point clear of their Premier League rivals.

Real Madrid struck late to drag themselves out of jail at AEK Athens and join PSG on maximum points from four games. Arsenal cannot catch those two sides tonight, but they do host Real next month.

Slavia are without their top scorer from the last two seasons, Tomas Chory, for rather unusual reasons. He has been banished from the club following a series of misdemeanours, the latest of which was showing the middle finger to the referee in a recent league game. Slavia have made it clear he won’t be playing for the club again, despite his importance to the team over the past few years.

Chory was also sent off for Czech Republic against Turkey at Euro 2024.

😬 Pandemonium after the final whistle! Czech Republic's Tomáš Chorý is shown a red card, with multiple others yellow carded, as players and staff from both sides clash 🟥 #Euro2024 | #CZETUR https://t.co/5xhR0Bwafa

Without meaning to be rude, I think it’s fair to say Slavia are not the most formidable opponent that Arsenal will face this season.

They are on a 22-game winless streak in the Champions League, dating back to 2007. If they don’t win tonight, they will equal the longest winless run in European Cup/Champions League history, shared with AEK Athens (1989-2006) and Steau Bucharest (2006-2013).

Slavia Prague XI: Domchak, Holes, Zima, Vlcek, Suleiman, Moses, Sadilek, Kubiak, Ayaosi, Sturm, Nowak

Subs: Markovic, Rezek, Chaloupek, N’Guessan, Chytil, Provod, Diakite, Kacor, Jurasek, Konecny, Barcot, Kotrba

Good evening from a chilly Prague, where Arsenal are looking for a repeat of the 3-0 victory they secured here exactly one year ago. It’s a remarkable coincidence that Mikel Arteta’s team have travelled to face Slavia Prague on November 4th in back-to-back years.

On that occasion last year, Max Dowman became the youngest player in Champions League history. He should get more minutes tonight from the bench, given that he is currently suspended from Premier League action following his controversial red card against Fleetwood last week.

That’s the most Arteta has rotated between a Premier League and Champions League game so far this season. Telling perhaps that Konsa, Gabriel and Rice – the team’s defensive bedrock – stay in place. But changes on both sides at full-back, and in the attacking midfield areas.

Arsenal XI: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Zubimendi, Merino; Madueke, Gyokeres, Eze

Subs: Kepa, Meslier, Saliba, Mosquera, Timber, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard, Guimaraes, Tzolis, Dowman, Havertz

Arsenal’s critics will still grumble about the style of victory, but, of all clubs, this is a team who have no obligation to play in a way that neutrals might enjoy. Arsenal spent so much of Arsene Wenger’s 22-year reign playing football that was mostly stylish but only sometimes effective in big games. Now they are mostly effective but only occasionally stylish on such occasions. If you asked all the travelling fans at Anfield which they prefer, you would receive an overwhelming response.

David Raya has kept a clean sheet in 54% of his Champions League starts (21 clean sheets from 39 starts), the best ratio of any goalkeeper to start at least 25 games in the competition. 🤯🇪🇸 https://t.co/A1Zpn8kJN9

Arsenal return to Slavia Prague for the third time under Mikel Arteta knowing that three points will be another step towards a top-eight finish in the Champions League league phase.

Arteta’s team were 4-0 winners in the Czech capital in a 2021 Europa League quarter-final second leg, and 3-0 victors at this stage of the Champions League a year ago. Bukayo Saka opened the scoring with a penalty before two second-half goals from Mikel Merino.

Paris-St Germain are top of the table on 12 points after their rout against Villarreal last night. Real Madrid, Liverpool and Real Betis are the three teams who have the chance to join them on maximum points. Arsenal will jump to 10 points with a win, above Bayern Munich, Sporting and Aston Villa at a minimum.

Slavia Prague are top of the Czech league and unbeaten after 13 games this season, but they are winless in the Champions League after fixtures against Lens, Sabah and Fernerbahce.

The fixture should be a presentable opportunity for Arteta to rotate his team, especially after a physically taxing game at Anfield where Arsenal showed their mettle to win at Liverpool’s home for the first time since 2012.

Arsenal’s second-string is very strong, though they did not cover themselves in glory at Fleetwood in the League Cup last week when Max Dowman was sent off. Given the 16-year-old is banned for another two Premier League games, and the attention Arteta’s touchline reaction to the red card attracted, one wonders if he might want to seize a chance to put Dowman back on the horse.

William Saliba’s return to full training is very welcome news, despite Ezri Konsa impressing in his absence. Saliba travelled with the squad to Prague, and could make his first appearance of the season following a back injury which flared up in France’s World Cup semi-final against Spain. With fixtures against Manchester City, Borussia Dortmund, Brentford, Spurs, Real Madrid, Bournemouth and Manchester United before the end of 2026 though, they will not want rush him.

Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Eberechi Eze are other players pushing for greater involvement from the start of matches.

#1181. How academic freedom is changing around the world — by the numbers

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Miryam Naddaf is a reporter for Nature in London.

University staff and students call for better funding for French education at a protest in Lyons.Credit: Antoine Boureau/Hans Lucas/AFP/Getty

Academic freedom is deteriorating globally, according to the Scholars at Risk (SAR) network, a human-rights organization based at New York University.

The network’s latest annual report documents 382 attacks on academic freedom by state authorities, affecting scholars, students and academic institutions in 59 countries and territories, between July 2025 and June 2026. That’s fewer incidents, but across more regions, than the previous year (which had seen 395 attacks in 49 countries and territories). The analysis, titled Free to Think 2026, defines an attack as a violent or fatal assault on scholars and students, wrongful prosecution or imprisonment, sacking or expulsion from institutions or restrictions to academic freedom or to travel.

Attacks on higher education are “about controlling the flow of information”, says Robert Quinn, founding executive director of SAR.

Sources: Free to Think 2026; V-Dem Dataset (https://go.nature.com/47UZF3P)

Tensions between universities and governments “represent some of the front lines of the debates and political clashes happening around the world”, says Mushfiq Mobarak, an economist at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut.

Other events counted in the SAR report include government interference with research topics or funding on ideological grounds. “While often justified in neutral terms — such as fiscal discipline, public accountability, or anti-discrimination — these interventions are often used to impose ideological control”, the SAR report explains.

But academic freedom has substantially improved in some places, notably Bangladesh (see ‘Freedom in figures’). Nature highlights five countries where scholars have experienced recent changes to their freedoms.

Data from the Academic Freedom Index Update 2026 report, published in March, show a steep decline in academic freedom in the United States (see ‘Rapid deterioration’). The trend is very troubling, says Quinn, who notes that it is not limited to the past five years. Its start precedes the return of US President Donald Trump to office in 2025. “The pressures on higher education are not limited to one election [or] one administration,” he says.

Sources: Free to Think 2026; Academic Freedom Index Update 2026

The country’s recent restrictions on immigration, such as travel bans and greater scrutiny of social-media accounts, contributed to a 35% drop in the number of international student visas granted by the United States during the summer of 2025 compared with that of 2024, according to Inside Higher Ed’s analysis of data released by the US State Department.

The government of Indonesia, led by President Prabowo Subianto since 2024, launched a violent crackdown on protests in 2025, which included raids on student demonstrations and suspending students thought to have anti-government views. The same year, the country’s military law was amended to allow officers to take roles in civic institutions without having to resign from the armed forces. Since then, researchers have reported an increased presence of military personnel on campuses and more government surveillance of universities.

Herlambang Wiratraman, who studies law and social justice at Gadjah Mada University in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, helped to establish a legal framework to protect academic freedom. He says that the situation in the country’s universities is getting worse amid intrusions by the current administration, including appointing presidents of universities and controlling research funds and agendas.

In contrast to the overall trend, in Hungary, a government elected in April led by Prime Minister Péter Magyar has rolled back various restrictions on university autonomy that were introduced during Viktor Orbán’s 16-year premiership.

During that time, many universities were managed by trusts run by boards whose members were often political appointees. In 2022, the Council of the European Union froze funds for 21 Hungarian universities and restricted access to the EU’s flagship research programme, Horizon Europe, and its exchange scheme Erasmus+. In October, the EU Council announced that it would restore full participation to these initiatives and release €4.2 billion (US$4.7 billion) in funding for Hungarian universities.

The SAR report says that the new administration in Hungary offers reason for cautious optimism.

“A lot of researchers and scientists are now joining the government,” says Balázs Lengyel, an economic geographer at the Centre for Economic and Regional Studies in Budapest. Many of them are being appointed “at the state-secretary level”.

#1180. Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy with 475 of 500 points as Barça reach five winners

Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsí, 19, has won Tuttosport's 2026 Golden Boy award for Europe's best under-21 player by a wide margin. The landslide puts a defender on top of a prize rarely won by one, and pushes Barcelona further clear as the club with the most winners.

This year’s vote was one-sided. No other candidate came close to the Barcelona defender.

The margin shows how settled the vote was. It also marks a rare win for a player in his position. Corriere dello Sport described him as only the second defender ever to win it. He succeeds PSG’s Désiré Doué, the 2025 winner.

Cubarsí now joins a club list that already featured Messi, Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal. Four of the five have come in the last six years. Pedri won in 2021, Gavi in 2022 and Lamine Yamal in 2024.

No player can win the award twice. Each Barcelona success therefore means a different young player reaching the top of the vote. The recent run points to a steady flow of talent into the first team.

The award caps a strong year for the defender. He was a big part of Barcelona’s LaLiga and Super Cup wins. He was also named young player of the tournament as Spain won the World Cup. He started all eight of Spain’s games there. FIFA’s Young Player Award made him the first defender to receive it. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final. They kept seven clean sheets and conceded only once, in a 2-1 quarter-final win over Belgium. The Golden Boy arrives just weeks after he narrowly missed out on the Kopa Trophy.

Cubarsí was not the only Barcelona name on the list. Three of Monday’s winners came from the club. Joan Laporta took the Best President award. Barça Femení B’s Giulia Galli won the Best Italian Golden Girl prize. Outside the club, the Best Agent prize went to Jorge Mendes.

Laporta’s prize puts the club’s president alongside its young defender in the same announcement. Galli’s award extends the club’s haul to its women’s set-up. Together, the three prizes give Barcelona recognition across the boardroom, the men’s first team and the women’s game.

𝗣𝗔𝗨 𝗖𝗨𝗕𝗔𝗥𝗦𝗜, 𝗚𝗢𝗟𝗗𝗘𝗡 𝗕𝗢𝗬 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲✨ pic.twitter.com/y4LljnnhOg

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 9, 2026

The timing suits both club and country. Barcelona sit top of LaLiga. Spain have a decider against England coming up. For Cubarsí, the award adds individual recognition to a season already built on trophies.

The prizes will be handed out at a ceremony in Turin on 14 December. All three of Barcelona’s awards become official at that ceremony.
